title: Filip Hrgovic: Moses Itauma 'amazing' but boxed 'like an amateur' in thrilling heavyweight fight at The O2
author: David Rivers
content:
Filip Hrgovic: Moses Itauma 'amazing' but boxed 'like an amateur' in thrilling heavyweight fight at The O2
Filip Hrgovic secured one of the biggest shocks in boxing this year after stopping an exhausted Moses Itauma in the ninth round at The O2; Hrgovic becomes Croatia's first-ever world heavyweight champion
Sunday 30 August 2026 11:02, UK
Filip Hrgovic praised Moses Itauma after his shock ninth-round stoppage but said his opponent had boxed “like an amateur”.
Hrgovic, 34, became Croatia's first world heavyweight champion at The O2 on Saturday night to win the vacant IBF heavyweight title.
Itauma, 21, who was unbeaten coming into the bout, was dominant in the first six rounds after landing a string of accurate blows.
But he became visibly exhausted as the fight progressed and he failed to find a way past Hrgovic's durable chin, with the seventh round being the first time in his career he had been past six rounds.
- Boxing in 2026: Key dates, results and upcoming schedule
- Get Sky Sports or stream boxing and more with no contract
The Croatian then pounced in the ninth round, which forced the Brit's corner to throw in the towel.
Following his win, Hrgovic hailed Itauma as the most talented fighter in the heavyweight division but said his boxing reminded him of the amateur ranks.
'I saw he was gassing'
Hrgovic said: "Let me be honest, he's amazing. I didn't know it was going to be so hard, I thought I was going to handle him easier.
"I was losing all the rounds. The kid is amazing, he was so fast, you don't see his punches coming.
"He doesn't hit so hard but he's fast. But since the first (round) I saw he was gassing out, he was boxing still like an amateur.
"He's inexperienced, I saw he was gassing out and I knew my only chance was to stay there to make him tired, to keep coming and to maybe stop him later on. That's what I did.
"I came to London, his hometown, against the most talented guy in the division and I beat all the odds.
"I want to be considered the best heavyweight in the world, and this is my time. I am the best. I am the present and he is the future.
"I want to fight for unification against Dubois or Agit Kabayel. I want to go for unification, that's what I want."
Itauma came into the fight lauded as one of the sport's brightest young talents after some early knockout wins.
But he will have to work on pacing himself for fights that go beyond the halfway point against durable opponents like Hrgovic.
Itauma taken to hospital but now home
Itauma was carried from the ring on a stretcher and taken to hospital following the stoppage as a precautionary measure.
On Sunday morning, a statement from Queensberry Promotions confirmed he had since left hospital and was home with his family.
The spokesperson said: "Moses is well. He left the hospital last night and is back at home with his family."
Promoter Frank Warren had earlier said: "That's what we always do to make sure because the most important thing is the boxer's health.
"He's there and he's in the best place. We'll see what happens when I've got a report. We'll obviously let everybody know.
"He's done something to his leg as well and he was quite tired. It was a high-paced, fast fight for both the guys. It was just edge of your seat stuff all the way through."
Itauma came into the fight hoping to be crowned Britain's youngest ever heavyweight world champion, but Warren said it was now unclear what his next move would be.
Warren added: "I don't know what he's going to say. I'm sure he's a fighting man. He showed that right to the end. At the end, that's the type of fight it was - they were standing there just letting bombs go.
"I don't even know how he feels mentally. Mentally, he's going to be completely down. We're going to have to talk to him and lift him and see what he's like.
"It's going to take some time. He's going to have a nice break. It's not even the time to talk about it with him at the moment.
"It's something we're probably doing in two weeks or even a month's time, see where we go with it."
Hrgovic must now take on the IBF's mandatory challenger Frank Sanchez.
summary: Filip Hrgovic secured a major upset by stopping an exhausted Moses Itauma in the ninth round at The O2 to win the vacant IBF heavyweight title, becoming Croatia's first-ever world champion in the division. Itauma dominated the early rounds with his speed, but tired as the fight progressed beyond six rounds for the first time in his career, prompting his corner to throw in the towel. Itauma was briefly taken to hospital as a precaution after being carried from the ring on a stretcher, but he has since returned home to his family.
key_points: Filip Hrgovic defeated Moses Itauma via a ninth-round stoppage to win the vacant IBF heavyweight title at The O2.
Hrgovic became Croatia's first-ever world heavyweight champion with the victory.
Moses Itauma dominated the first six rounds with fast, accurate punches before becoming visibly exhausted.
Itauma was taken to the hospital as a precautionary measure following the bout and has since returned home.
Hrgovic stated his desire to pursue a unification fight against Daniel Dubois or Agit Kabayel.

title: Filip Hrgovic stuns Britain’s Moses Itauma to claim IBF world heavyweight title
author: Donald McRae
content:
Moses Itauma’s hopes of becoming the second-youngest world heavyweight champion in history lay in ruins after the extraordinarily tough and resilient Filip Hrgovic stopped him in the ninth round of their IBF title fight. Yet, until the latter stages of round eight, the sheer speed and dextrous power of the Briton had dominated the contest, with the Croat being dropped in the second and caught again and again by jolting combinations.
The fight changed course when Itauma’s stamina suddenly dipped and he began to weave in woozy fatigue as Hrgovic fought back with granite-like determination. Itauma could not withstand the dark storm rolling over him in the ninth and he sank back against the ropes as Hrgovic opened up with renewed conviction. Just as the referee stepped in to stop the fight, Ben Davison, Itauma’s trainer, also sent a white towel sailing sadly over the listing ropes to save his man from a knockout.
The shocking twist was too much for the 21-year-old and he left the ring on a stretcher, apparently having injured his knee. But the damage was done by the remarkable fightback from his opponent, who made his own significant slice of boxing history. The admirable Hrgovic is the first world heavyweight champion from Croatia – a country that has no real boxing heritage.
The shock result was also a sobering reminder that, for all Itauma’s obvious skill, a heavyweight tyro is always vulnerable to a world-class opponent who simply refuses to surrender. Itauma’s inexperience also cost him badly for, rather than boxing with more care and staying out of trouble from the eighth round onwards, he allowed himself to be caught up in a slugfest.
Before the late dramatics, Itauma walked with calm solemnity to the ring, seemingly unmoved by the fact that the crammed and partisan crowd had begun singing his name in raucous harmony even before he left his dressing room.
![Filip Hrgovic head is knocked back by a right hand from Moses Itauma](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/791bdfb01ab5442eeefb31378d47f18698610a3d/0_0_4583_3056/master/4583.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Fighting out of a southpaw stance, Itauma landed the first meaningful punch, a sweeping right hand. Moving with menacing intent Itauma clipped Hrgovic with fast and cuffing blows. His speed was striking as he backed up the bigger man with a shuddering right cross which nailed and shook up Hrgovic.
Itauma missed with a scything left early in the second but Hrgovic walked almost immediately on to a jolting short right hook which dropped him to the canvas for a count of eight. Hrgovic fought back near the end of the round only for Itauma to produce another blistering combination.
A sharp left snapped back Hrgovic’s head at the start of the third, as sweat glistened on the faces and torsos of both men. Itauma switched to the body, sinking a cruel blow to Hrgovic’s gut, but the Croat refused to wilt. His vociferous supporters at ringside began screaming their support as he had a measure of success for the first time in the fight to prove that his ambition remained undimmed.
Itauma began to grimace occasionally as the pace of the fight began to leave its mark. A beautiful short left snaked through Hrgovic’s defence in the fifth but the older man marched forward with stoic determination. Itauma was starting to breathe heavily and he had to use a glove to slip his black gum shield back into his mouth. It was the first real sign of distress in Itauma’s previously impassive expression. But at the bell a spiteful uppercut rocked back Hrgovic’s head on the plinth of his massive neck.
The cut about Hrgovic’s right eye began to seep with a tickle of blood. But just before the bell Hrgovic landed some heavy shots. Itauma absorbed them and fired back as the fight really caught fire.
Itauma had never boxed more than six rounds before and he entered uncharted territory in the seventh. But he again forced Hrgovic on to the back foot and landed some deft combinations.
after newsletter promotion
![The referee raises his hand to stop the fight as Moses Itauma’s team throw the towel in](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/f31fb1467667b1df24eb4407b782c95fa5366819/0_0_4839_3274/master/4839.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Hrgovic ate one meaty blow after another in the eighth round but was resolute as ever. Itauma looked desperately weary as Hrgovic, unbelievably, rallied again. He would soon overwhelm the exhausted youngster and finish a remarkable resurgence.
Throughout an intriguing fight week, the 34-year-old Hrgovic had tried to unsettle his complex rival by suggesting that becoming a world heavyweight champion at such a young age would be “bad for his soul”. Itauma, who is so suspicious of fame, engaged fully with those doubts about his readiness for sporting celebrity. It was almost as if the callow prodigy was uncertain, deep down, whether his world title shot had arrived too early.
Hrgovic was always going to provide an acid test of Itauma’s much lauded credentials. The experienced Croat had lost only one previous bout in his nine years as a professional. It had been expected that he would not match Itauma’s deft footwork, fast hands, clarity of thinking and the kind of power that is impressive because it arrives from such dizzying and unexpected angles.
But Itauma, instead, was rendered helpless by Hrgovic’s superior stamina and bludgeoning will and self-belief. “Let me tell you something,” Hrgovic said afterwards. “It was not me tonight. It was Jesus Christ in me. Holy Spirit. Father, Son and the Holy Spirit. It was not me. I was losing every round. I was outboxed. And I don’t know from where I got energy in that ninth round. And it was really not my strength. It was the Holy Spirit.”
He then turned his attention to his fallen opponent. “He’s an amazing fighter,” Hrgovic said of Itauma. “I want to thank him for accepting this fight, to give me a chance to become a new superstar in the heavyweight division. I’m the present and he’s definitely the future.”
Itauma is obviously more than young enough to come back from such crushing disappointment but it is Hrgovic who will celebrate victory in the weeks and months to come. The new world champion administered a chastening lesson in the harsh and unforgiving realities of heavyweight boxing.
summary: Filip Hrgovic stopped Moses Itauma in the ninth round of their IBF world heavyweight title fight after a dramatic comeback. Itauma had dominated the early rounds with his speed and power, knocking Hrgovic down in the second. However, Itauma's stamina faded in the later rounds, allowing the resilient Hrgovic to overwhelm him and force a stoppage. With this victory, Hrgovic became Croatia's first world heavyweight champion.
key_points: Filip Hrgovic defeated Moses Itauma via a ninth-round TKO to claim the IBF world heavyweight title.
Itauma dominated the early stages of the fight, landing fast combinations and dropping Hrgovic in the second round.
Itauma's stamina dipped significantly in the later rounds, exposing his inexperience as he entered uncharted territory past the sixth round.
Hrgovic's relentless determination and late surge overwhelmed the exhausted younger fighter, prompting the referee and Itauma's trainer to stop the bout.
Hrgovic made boxing history by becoming the first world heavyweight champion from Croatia.

title: Itauma vs Hrgovic: Briton punches himself out and is stopped in round nine
author: Kal Sajad
content:
![Filip Hrgovic lands a punch on Moses Itauma](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/983/cpsprodpb/7f9c/live/a595bab0-a3fe-11f1-94f0-8d62ae00a5eb.jpg)
Filip Hrgovic has picked up 15 of his 20 wins by stoppage
- Published
Filip Hrgovic ripped up the script and shattered Moses Itauma's world-title dream as the Briton appeared to punch himself out in an extraordinary heavyweight contest in London.
Itauma, 21, controlled most of the fight and scored a second-round knockdown but faded as his relentless output caught up with him.
Hrgovic weathered the storm and piled on the pressure in the ninth. With Itauma barely able to stand, his legs unsteady and body swaying before slumping in the corner, his team threw in the towel.
Itauma - who needed medical attention before leaving the arena on a stretcher - had been a heavy favourite after tearing through his first 14 opponents and was spoken about as heavyweight boxing's next superstar.
"He is the best I have been in the ring with, but he needs more experience. I knew I was losing the round, but I knew that I had the pace in my favour. He needs more experience, but he is one of a kind," Hrgovic said.
"From the first round, I saw his gassing out. He started fast. I knew he was going to gas out. I knew when my chance came I needed to push. That is what I did."
With the vacant IBF title on the line, victory would have made Itauma the second-youngest world champion in the division's history.
Instead, his inexperience began to show as his Croatian opponent - an Olympic bronze medallist whose only previous professional defeat came against Daniel Dubois - survived everything Itauma threw at him before completing a remarkable turnaround.
Hrgovic's remarkable turnaround as Itauma shows inexperience
![Filip Hrgovic has the IBF heavyweight title around his waist and holds up his fists](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/892/cpsprodpb/9a7e/live/7cc8c440-a405-11f1-99ed-fd7767e0b3d2.jpg)
Filip Hrgovic is the first heavyweight world champion from Croatia
Hrgovic - wearing the red and white checks of his country - made his entrance first to a wall of boos, before the mood inside the O2 Arena flipped as Itauma emerged to a huge roar - taking his time and soaking up the reception.
The crowd had made its allegiances clear after a fiery build-up which included Itauma shoving Hrgovic, the Zagreb man slapping him back and plenty of verbal sparring.
Itauma came out with real intent, landing straight lefts from his southpaw stance. Hrgovic is known for his durability but struggled to keep pace with the Briton's speed early on.
Early in the second, a right hook knocked Hrgovic off-balance and his glove touched the canvas. Oasis star Noel Gallagher and boxing legend Prince Naseem Hamed were among those watching as the crowd gasped at almost every Itauma punch, whether it landed or not.
But by the end of the third, Itauma - who had boxed just 26 professional rounds before his first world-title fight - was already breathing heavily.
There had also been questions over his chin, simply because it had never really been tested. Hrgovic began landing the occasional heavy shot but Itauma took them well and fired straight back.
A fight in the crowd momentarily took attention away from the action in the fifth before an Itauma uppercut in the closing seconds brought the focus back to the ring.
Itauma continued to fire combinations but Hrgovic was barely budging. A huge right landed on the bell in the sixth and another followed in the seventh, yet the Croatian simply walked through them.
The Briton was well ahead but, rather than box his way towards victory, he continued to chase the knockout. A flurry in the eighth backed Hrgovic on to the ropes and had him in trouble, but Itauma was grimacing between exchanges and looking increasingly spent.
By now the danger was clear. Hrgovic came out with renewed purpose in the ninth and landed a thudding right which sent Itauma staggering backwards, almost through the ropes.
The youngster somehow stayed upright but his legs had gone. Hrgovic continued to press and when Itauma slumped into his corner, exhausted and barely able to defend himself, referee Howard Foster waved off the contest as the towel came in.
Hrgovic crashes the party - what next for Itauma?
![Moses Itauma is held on the ropes by the referee as Filip Hrgovic watches](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/819/cpsprodpb/d2c2/live/a13c9590-a405-11f1-99ed-fd7767e0b3d2.jpg)
Moses Itauma had stopped 12 of his previous 14 opponents
Hrgovic admitted he had been "outboxed" but leaves London as Croatia's first heavyweight world champion, with Frank Sanchez waiting as the IBF mandatory challenger.
A unification fight could follow, with Daniel Dubois holding the WBO title and set to face Fabio Wardley again in October.
For Itauma, this was supposed to be a coronation.
Instead, he leaves the O2 Arena with questions over whether the step up came too soon.
He has time to rebuild and there will be a strong feeling that, with a little more experience, this night could have ended very differently.
Londoner Dubois was stopped by Joe Joyce as an unbeaten 23-year-old before going on to become a two-time world champion. Itauma has even more time on his side.
"He's an amazing fighter," Hrgovic said. "I am the present. He is definitely the future."
Promoter Frank Warren suggested Itauma was carrying a leg injury in the final round but backed him to return.
"Moses gave everything," he added. "He has to go back to the drawing board and he can come again."
The expectation around Itauma will not disappear entirely overnight but the aura of invincibility has gone.
Itauma showed heart in defeat - Brown
summary: Filip Hrgovic stopped 21-year-old Briton Moses Itauma in the ninth round of their heavyweight contest in London to claim the vacant IBF title. Itauma controlled the early rounds and scored a knockdown in the second, but he faded due to a relentless output and inexperience. Hrgovic weathered the storm, capitalized on Itauma's exhaustion, and secured the stoppage when Itauma's team threw in the towel.
key_points: Filip Hrgovic defeated Moses Itauma by a ninth-round stoppage to win the vacant IBF heavyweight title.
Itauma controlled the early part of the fight and knocked Hrgovic down in the second round.
Itauma faded due to his high-output pace, allowing Hrgovic to capitalize and overwhelm him in the ninth round.
The victory makes Hrgovic the first heavyweight world champion from Croatia.
Itauma required medical attention after the bout and left the arena on a stretcher.

title: Filip Hrgović completes astonishing comeback to stun Moses Itauma and win IBF title – live reaction
author: Bryan Armen Graham; Donald McRae
content:
Here’s how Itauma and Hrgović measure up ahead of tonight’s main event. Itauma is the younger man by 13 years and gives away an inch and a half in height and three inches in reach, but he will enter the ring as the heavier fighter. The 21-year-old tipped the scales at 241.7lb, compared with 232.6lb for Hrgovic. The Croatian brings a significant edge in professional experience, having boxed 105 rounds to Itauma’s 31.
What an extraordinary turnaround at the O2. Itauma looked sensational early, his speed and power giving Hrgović all sorts of problems, and he dropped the Croatian in the second round. But Hrgović absorbed everything the 21-year-old threw at him and simply refused to go away.
Then the fight turned. Itauma began to tire badly after the sixth and Hrgović’s experience, chin and persistence took over. By the ninth, Itauma was completely spent. Hrgović battered him around the ring until Ben Davison threw in the towel, completing a remarkable comeback.
It is a stunning upset – and a historic one. Hrgovic becomes Croatia’s first heavyweight world champion, while Itauma suffers his first professional defeat after being anointed by so many as the division’s next king before he had even won a belt.
Hrgović is battering a completely sapped Itauma in the opening minute. Itauma missing a lot of punches and missing them wildly. Hrgović lands a massive right hand that sends Itauma reeling into the ropes. Itauma is exhuasted! Hrgović pours it on, unloading shot after shot on Itauma and he can barely stay on his feet! Are they going to stop this fight? Itauma’s corner has thrown in the towel! Unbelievable!
Moses Itauma’s corner throws in the towel as referee Howard Foster stops his IBF heavyweight title fight against Filip Hrgović at the O2 Arena. Photograph: Richard Pelham/Getty Images
Filip Hrgović celebrates after knocking down Moses Itauma during their vacant IBF heavyweight title fight at the O2 Arena. Photograph: Steven Paston/PA
Itauma begins to pour it on in the second half of the round, battering Hrgović around the ring and opening a cut over his eye. Forty-five seconds to go and Itauma is pummeling away, going for the stoppage. The referee is taking a closer look. But Hrgović fires back! He’s battering an exhausted Itauma, who sold out for the stoppage and is breathing heavy! This is a live fight!
Itauma is into the seventh round for the first time in his career. Itauma continues to score to the head and body with a higher workrate, but Hrgović is taking the shots well and both men look equally pressed for stamina. Itauma clips Hrgović with a right hand in the final seconds that moves him backwards.
Itauma is outthrowing and outlanding his opponent to the head and the body. Hrgović rallies back nicely in the final minute, chin-checking Itauma with a right hand and following it up with three or four more blows upstairs. But the 21-year-old closes strong again, landing another big shot at the bell.
Speed kills. It’s been the difference in this fight so far. Hrgović looks exhausted. The only strategy appears to be enduring the punishment around long enough to test Itauma’s stamina. Itauma detonates a concussive uppercut on Hrgović’s chin in the final seconds of the round but Hrgović somehow remains upright.
Hrgović appears lightyears more relaxed and settled than in the first round, but he’s been cut and is still in there with a dangerous foe who’s got the whole arena behind him. The strategy is clearly to let Itauma gas out and it’s not a bad thought, but Ituama is still outthrowing and outlanding him. What a chin from Hrgović. How many more of these shots can he take?
The pace has slowed markedly into the third. Hrgović is coming forward now and scoring with power shots including a thudding right cross, but Itauma takes it well. The closest round of the fight and Hrgović has done just enough to shade it.
Hrgović is down early in the round! Itauma catches him with a counter right hook for a flash knockdown. The Croatian quickly makes his feet, but the chasm in hand speed between these two is alarming. Then Hrgović, who has been almost completely shut down for a round and a half, finally starts letting his hands go in the final minute. Perhaps he’s beginning to get a read on Itauma’s timing. Still, another terrific round for the youngster.
There’s the bell! The meet in the center of the ring and it’s a big right hook early from Itauma that lands on Hrgović’s temple. Deafening cheers for Itauma from the rollicking crowd. Good punch variety early for Itauma, who is really on the front foot here throwing loaded shots from all angles. Hrgović has yet to really get anything going through the first 90 seconds. A heavy left hand from Itauma lands and sends Hrgović reeling backwards. Another head-body combination from Itauma. Hrgović looks wobbly. A dream start from the 21-year-old from Chatham.
The waiting is over. The final instructions have been given by referee Howard Foster, the seconds are out and we’ll pick it up with round-by-round coverage from here!
The fighters are making their entrances for the main event. First out is Hrgović, emerging to Geni Kameni, the rousing Croatian nationalist anthem by the controversial rock singer Thompson. Now here comes Itauma, making his way to the ring in a black sleeveless vest to a medley of Sister Nancy’s Bam Bam and Crystal Waters’ Gypsy Woman (She’s Homeless). He’s moving with purpose, practically at a canter.
Moses Itauma makes his ringwalk before facing Filip Hrgovic for the vacant IBF heavyweight title at the O2 Arena. Photograph: Steven Paston/PA
One final newsy note before Itauma and Hrgovic make their ringwalks. Chantelle Cameron has just beaten Mikaela Mayer by unanimous decision in Birmingham to become the unified three-belt champion at 154lb. Cameron prevailed by scores of 97-93, 97-93 and 96-94 after 10 rounds. Alycia Baumgardner calls it her favorite fight of the year! Claressa Shields wants the winner and the loser!
Meanwhile, back at the O2, we’re going through the national anthems of Croatia and the United Kingdom ahead of the main event fighter entrances.
It’s a night for the heavyweights, with various big men at contrasting stages of their careers in attendance. Agit Kabayel, Daniel Dubois, Fabio Wardley, Joe Joyce and Derek Chisora are at ringside. I hope we don’t ever see the last two in a fight again but Dubois and Wardley, who waged a thrilling battle earlier this year, have just announced the date of their rematch. I hope Wardley has had enough time to recover from the damage he absorbed in May. Kabayel, meanwhile, was gifted the WBC world title in June, after Oleksander Usyk gave up his belts.
Meanwhile, at lightweight, Sam Noakes was too young and fresh for Denys Berinchyk, the 38-year-old Ukrainian, in the last bout on the undercard, winning a wide decision on points. And Noakes did make his ring walk to the mighty Dolly Parton.
Not too long now before Moses Itauma and Filip Hrgović …
Frank Warren has just made some news from the ring at the O2. Daniel Dubois and Fabio Wardley will meet again for the WBO heavyweight title at the same venue on 17 October.
Wardley has exercised his rematch clause after their bloody first encounter in Manchester, when he floored Dubois twice in the opening round before Dubois took control and ultimately won. The roles will be reversed this time: Dubois enters as champion, Wardley as challenger.
Also announced: Northern Ireland’s Anthony Cacace will defend his WBA junior-lightweight title against Liverpool’s Nick Ball on 19 December in Belfast.
Fabio Wardley (left) and Daniel Dubois (right) pose with promoter Frank Warren after their WBO heavyweight title rematch was announced for 17 October at the O2 Arena. Photograph: Richard Pelham/Getty Images
Sam Noakes has scored the biggest win of his career, outclassing former world champion Denys Berinchyk to win a 10-round unanimous decision. The 29-year-old from Kent controlled the fight throughout, winning by scores of 100-90, 99-91 and 98-92.
That’s it for the undercard at the O2. The final countdown to Moses Itauma v Filip Hrgović is on.
Sam Noakes (right) lands a punch on Denys Berinchyk during their lightweight fight at the O2 Arena. Photograph: Richard Pelham/Getty Images
Elsewhere in England, Caroline Dubois has retained her WBC and WBO lightweight titles with a unanimous-decision win over Amelia Moore in Birmingham. Dubois dropped Moore in the fifth round before the challenger rallied to make the fight more competitive than the 99-90, 99-90 and 98-91 scorecards suggested.
Afterwards, Dubois became embroiled in a heated exchange with Alycia Baumgardner, the WBA, WBO and IBF champion at 130lb, adding the latest chapter to the simmering war of words between the promotional stablemates that has been building for the past year.
Caroline Dubois (right) clashes with Alycia Baumgardner (left) after retaining her WBC and WBO lightweight titles with a unanimous-decision win over Amelia Moore in Birmingham. Photograph: Matthew Lewis/Getty Images
There was no shortage of needle at Friday’s weigh-in, where the bad blood that has simmered throughout fight week finally boiled over. After an expletive-laden face-off at Spitalfields Market, Itauma shoved Hrgović off the stage, sending the Croatian stumbling backwards. Hrgovic quickly climbed back up and struck Itauma in the face before security separated them.
“I just lost it a little bit,” Itauma admitted afterwards, later adding: “I had a little itch, and I just had to scratch it.” The flashpoint followed days of Hrgović provoking the 21-year-old, repeatedly calling him a “kid” and “delusional” and promising to “send him back to high school”.
There is a gnawing contradiction at the heart of Saturday’s promotion. Itauma is being put forth as boxing’s next big star, with the chance to become the youngest world heavyweight champion since Mike Tyson nearly 40 years ago.
Yet in the US, Itauma v Hrgović costs $59.99 on Dazn PPV, while UK viewers must fork over £24.99 and Australians A$39.99. Those prices are on top of a standard Dazn subscription, although the fight is included for subscribers to the more expensive Ultimate tier. This is not an unfamiliar arrangement in modern boxing, but it is a strange way to build an audience around a 21-year-old fighter who is supposed to help carry the sport into its next era.
If boxing wants Itauma to become a mainstream attraction, surely the priority should be getting him in front of as many eyeballs as possible. Instead, potential new fans are being asked to clear multiple financial barriers simply to watch him fight.
“Putting a fight like Moses Itauma v Filip Hrgovic this weekend behind the pay-per-view wall is actually criminal,” Helwani said. “That is truly criminal. What are you doing? Enough already. Stop putting these fights behind multiple paywalls. They did it last weekend too with the López-Romero fight. You want people to fall in love with these fighters? You got to make them accessible.”
Correction: there’s one more preliminary fight before Noakes v Berinchyk. And it was a quick one. Nelson Hysa, aka the Albanian Eagle, just made quick work of the badly overmatched Thomas Narmo, scoring a brutal technical knockout early in the second round.
Nelson Hysa knocks out Thomas Narmo during their heavyweight non-title fight at the O2 Arena. Photograph: Richard Pelham/Getty Images
The arena looks pretty close to full which is a positive surprise. There was speculation earlier in the week that ticket sales had been a little sluggish and when I arrived just before seven this evening they were still selling seats to people who had just walked up to the 02. This is only Moses Itauma’s 15th fight and, while his face has been plastered across London’s buses the past few weeks, he is still a 21-year-old fighter who is at the start of his ascent to elite-level boxing.
This could be the fight, against a tough and ambitious Filip Hrgović, which could mark the big breakthrough for Itauma. At the same time there is a risk that the callow prodigy might be exposed. I reckon that Itauma will be too good for Hrgović, but the atmosphere is building and there is a nice little frisson of uncertainty in the air.
Here’s how Itauma and Hrgović measure up ahead of tonight’s main event. Itauma is the younger man by 13 years and gives away an inch and a half in height and three inches in reach, but he will enter the ring as the heavier fighter. The 21-year-old tipped the scales at 241.7lb, compared with 232.6lb for Hrgovic. The Croatian brings a significant edge in professional experience, having boxed 105 rounds to Itauma’s 31.
Here’s where things stand in the order of play. Constantin Ursu has just retained his British and Commonwealth welterweight titles with an eighth-round stoppage of Ben Vaughan. The unbeaten champion was pushed hard by a game Vaughan before a severe cut over his right eyebrow brought the contest to a premature end at the O2. Ursu improves to 16-0 (7 KOs) with the TKO win.
That leaves one more undercard fight before tonight’s main event: a scheduled 12-round lightweight scrap between Sam Noakes and Denys Berinchyk.
Ben Vaughan (right) lands a punch on Constantin Ursu during their British and Commonwealth welterweight title fight at the O2 Arena. Photograph: Richard Pelham/Getty Images
Hello and welcome to London’s O2 Arena, where we are counting down to one of the more intriguing heavyweight attractions of the year and, just maybe, the launch of a new era in boxing’s bellwether division.
Moses Itauma is only 21 years old, unbeaten in 14 paying fights and already being spoken about in the sort of glowing terms normally reserved for fighters who have spent years at or near the top of the division. Tonight the prodigiously gifted southpaw from Chatham can become the second-youngest heavyweight champion in history, behind only Mike Tyson, when he faces Filip Hrgović for the vacant International Boxing Federation title at the O2 Arena.
The hype is not difficult to understand. Itauma has speed uncommon for a man his size, concussive power and an ability to attack from angles that Barry Jones believes separates him from almost every other heavyweight. But for everything we have seen, there is plenty we haven’t. Itauma has boxed only 31 professional rounds. He has never been dragged into the deep waters of a difficult fight, where Andy Lee believes the questions surrounding him become less technical than psychological.
Britain’s Moses Itauma can become the youngest world heavyweight champion since Mike Tyson nearly 40 years ago. Photograph: Richard Pelham/Getty Images
That is where Hrgović comes in. The 34-year-old Croatian has been a professional for nine years and lost only once (to Daniel Dubois in 2024). He has spent the buildup dismissing Itauma as a “delusional kid”, even suggesting that becoming champion so young could “ruin his soul”. It’s an idea Itauma has not entirely dismissed. He has spoken candidly this week about the burden of sudden fame and his desire to “start off like Mike Tyson started, but not end up how Mike Tyson ended”.
It should be mentioned the widely recognized king of the division is still Oleksandr Usyk, the unbeaten former undisputed heavyweight champion from Ukraine who relinquished his remaining world title belts in June but insists he has not retired. But with the old order beginning to clear, Itauma is ideally placed to collect the spoils and establish himself as the leading candidate to inherit Usyk’s throne when the time comes.
We’ll have round-by-round updates, key moments and instant reaction in this space. Stay with us.
summary: Filip Hrgović completed a remarkable comeback to defeat Moses Itauma and win the vacant IBF heavyweight title at the O2 Arena. After surviving an early onslaught and a second-round knockdown from the 21-year-old, Hrgović used his experience and durability as Itauma tired badly in the later rounds. The fight was ultimately stopped in the ninth round when Itauma's corner threw in the towel, handing Itauma his first professional defeat and making Hrgović Croatia's first heavyweight world champion.
key_points: Moses Itauma dropped Filip Hrgović in the second round and controlled the early portion of the fight with his speed and power.
Hrgović absorbed heavy punishment and capitalized as Itauma began to tire significantly after the sixth round.
The referee stopped the fight in the ninth round after Itauma's corner threw in the towel following a relentless assault by Hrgović.
The victory marks a historic first for Croatia, crowning Hrgović as the nation's first heavyweight world champion while handing Itauma his initial professional loss.

title: Tottenham Hotspur v Newcastle: How the players rated
author: Ciaran Kelly
content:
![Tottenham's Sandro Tonali challenges Newcastle's Anthony Elanga during their Premier League match at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in north London.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1024/cpsprodpb/bb70/live/04e8e750-a3d5-11f1-9323-c53d27c293d7.jpg)
Sandro Tonali joined Spurs from Newcastle United in a deal worth up to Â£100m earleir this summer
- Published
Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa fired Newcastle United to a 2-0 victory against Tottenham Hotspur.
Here's how I rated the players at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and you can see how you scored them below.
Tottenham Hotspur
Spurs didn't deserve Newcastle defeat - De Zerbi
Antonin Kinsky: Unlike his countryman, Lukas Hornicek, the Spurs goalkeeper had nothing to do in the first half but could only watch on as Elanga's shot went in off the post after the break before Wissa's improvised effort made it 2-0. 5
Archie Gray: Can never fault his effort but is he at his very best at right-back? 5
Micky van de Ven: The captain's first start of the season. Picked up a needless early booking, but went on to make a crucial sliding challenge to deny Wissa inside the box. 6
Jan Paul van Hecke: Got back to make a block to deny Willock. Comfort in possession allowed Spurs to bypass Newcastle press. Went close with header. 6
Andy Robertson: Carried a threat going forward in the first half but could not prevent Dedic winning a header to set up Elanga's goal. 5
Rodrigo Bentancur: Work often goes unseen. Broke up play and won ball back on a number of occasions. 5
Sandro Tonali: A shaky start as he came up against his former club for the first time. Clearly still building up fitness. At fault in build up to both goals. Ironically cheered by away fans as he came off. 4
Mateus Fernandes: First Premier League start for club. Always looked to be positive and deliveries from corners caused one or two problems in first half. 5
Pedro Porro: The World Cup winner played further forward on the right wing and had a couple of openings, seeing a shot blocked by Hall and a dipping volley go just over. 5
Omar Marmoush: Debutant was quickly parachuted into starting line-up, having tormented Newcastle so many times before with Manchester City. Hit side netting on volley. Smart reverse pass created opening for Robertson. 6
Mathys Tel: Saw one stinging effort well-saved, but also frustrated the crowd by giving the ball away. 4
Subs:
Kudus (on 68, Tel): Welcome return after being sidelined since January with a serious quad injury 5
Moore (on 68, Gray): 5
Udogie (on 68, Robertson) 5
Dominic Solanke (on 75, Tonali): 5
Subs not used: Dubravka, Senesi, Gallagher, Bergvall, Davies
Newcastle United
Newcastle showed 'full commitment' in Spurs win - Jaissle
Lukas Hornicek: Made saves to keep out Tel, Robertson and van Hecke's efforts when Newcastle were under pressure in the first half. His save from van Hecke's header left head coach Matthias Jaissle clenching his fists on the touchline. 7
Amar Dedic: Another impressive all-round performance from the summer signing little more than a week-and-a-half into his Newcastle career. Great knock-down header to set up first goal. Tino Livramento faces a real battle to win back his place. 7
Malick Thiaw: Captain again in Dan Burn's absence. A proper old-fashioned tussle with Marmoush at times, who kept him on his toes. 6
Sven Botman: Had a shaky pre-season but looking more assured. Appears to be benefitting from a run of games with the same back four. 6
Lewis Hall: Made a huge last-ditch block inside the box to prevent Porro from getting a shot away in first half. Defensively solid and no penalty fears this time. 7
Nico Gonzalez: An impressive debut. Kept composure even after booking. A stunning cross-field ball in the build up to Elanga's goal. 8
Lewis Miley: Goes about his work quietly but keeps the ball so well. 7
Anthony Elanga: Looks a reborn player full of confidence under Jaissle. Scored his second goal in two games with a smart turn and finish in off the post. His was the name repeatedly sung by the away supporters. 7.
Joe Willock: Made an instant impact after coming off the bench against Liverpool, but not as effective as a starter on Saturday. Got one of biggest cheers from Newcastle fans for a meaty challenge on Tonali. 5
Harvey Barnes: Fresh from scoring two goals in the midweek win over West Brom in the Carabao Cup, but did not offer same threat this time. Fired one effort way over and failed to pick out a team-mate on one promising breakaway after his cutback went straight into traffic. 5
Yoane Wissa: Led the line in injured William Osula's absence and repeatedly dropped deep to help his side. Clever overhead kick sealed the win. 7
Subs:
Sean Steur (on 71, Gonzalez): Sent in teasing deliver with corner in build up to Wissa's goal. 7
Nick Woltemade (on 71, Willock): Header set up Newcastle's second from Steur's corner. 7
Subs not used: Jaouen, Schar, Bamba, Toure, Murphy, Ramsey, Shahar
How did you rate the players?
Player of the match
After the opportunity to rate players has closed, the score displayed represents the average from all the submissions by BBC Sport users.
summary: Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa secured a 2-0 victory for Newcastle United against Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League. Elanga opened the scoring with a shot that went in off the post after the break, and Wissa sealed the win with an improvised overhead kick. The match featured notable performances, including an impressive debut by Newcastle's Nico Gonzalez and a difficult outing for former Newcastle player Sandro Tonali playing for Spurs.
key_points: Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa scored to give Newcastle United a 2-0 win over Tottenham Hotspur.
Sandro Tonali faced his former club for the first time and struggled, being at fault in the buildup to both goals.
Newcastle debutant Nico Gonzalez delivered an impressive performance, including a key cross-field ball for the opening goal.
Goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek made crucial first-half saves to help maintain Newcastle's clean sheet under pressure.

title: Bournemouth 1-1 Everton, Coventry 0-1 Hull and more: football clockwatch – as it happened
author: Sarah Rendell; Jacob Steinberg
content:
Thank you for joining us for the clockwatch with some great goals on display. Bournemouth miss out on all three points by conceding a late equalsier against Everton and Hull City continue their perfect start to the season with a 1-0 win over Conventry. To catch up on all of that action have a read of the reports below. Enjoy the rest of the weekend and keep up to date with Spurs v Newcastle on our blog.
The Premier League action is not over today with Tottenham v Newcastle kicking off at 5.30pm BST. For all of the updates from that one, have a read of this:
Coventry and Hull are both newly promoted sides but they are having a very different start to the season. Hull have conceded no goals and scored three, Coventry have concided four goals and scored none.
Hull City are second in the Premier League after they compound their opening win of the season with a late winner from Millar. Coventry will be frustrated and they may come to rue this result come the end of the season.
Liam Millar celebrates with the Hull City fans after the final whistle. Photograph: Tony O'Brien/Reuters
Coventry 0-1 Hull City, 90 + 4 min: Can Coventry copy Everton and find an equaliser? Well their fans don’t think so as hundreds head for the exit before full-time.
The Alex Scott first half goal looked like it was going to be enough for Bournemouth with another of their chances not converted but Everton snuck an equaliser in injury time. A thoroughly entertaining clash.
Coventry 0-1 Hull City, 85 min: I know it is early doors in the Premier League and Coventry could equalise or even win this game but as things stand Hull are second in the table. They are still among favourites to be relegated but what a start for the club after a decade out of the top-flight.
Coventry 0-1 Hull City, 83 min: Belloumi does so well in the build-up too in that goal. He was being pulled but his pass made it possible for Millar to be released. Great goal.
Millar has a second chance in front of goal and he wasn’t going to miss this time. A great finish and Hull City look like they are taking two wins from two at the start of this league season.
Hull City's Liam Millar slots home from the edge of the box to open the scoring. Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/Reuters
Liam Millar (second right) celebrates with his teammates. Photograph: Paul Marriott/Shutterstock
Coventry 0-0 Hull City, 81 min: Another fun fact for you, in both games involving these two clubs in the Championship this season it ended 0-0. New league, same result.
Bournemouth 1-0 Everton, 81 min: Pickford has made a good save to stop Bournemouth from doublign their lead. It is Rayan who had a low shot that was palmed wide by the England international and Evanilson can’t put the rebound ball in the back of the net.
Coventry 0-0 Hull City, 76 min: The rain has stopped and the sun is now shining in Coventry and it doesn’t feel like a coincidence that has happened since Sakamoto has been on. He really had livened up Coventry but like his teammates, he is yet to be clinical in front of goal.
Lucas Herrington of Hull City closes down Tatsuhiro Sakamoto of Coventry City. Photograph: Andy Sumner/Focus Images Ltd/Shutterstock
Bournemouth 1-0 Everton, 75 min: Beto had a chance but there was some great defensive work as the ball was kicked away just as he was lining up to shoot.
Coventry 0-0 Hull City, 71 min: Coventry have a corner but the opportunity is wasted. This game does have all the air of one that a team could steal the result at the death.
Bournemouth 1-0 Everton, 69 min: The attacking intensity in this fixture has dramatically dropped in this second half and the Toffees will need to create something tangible soon to get back into this one.
Coventry 0-0 Hull City, 63 min: Coventry win a corner, can they find the opener? No they can’t. It was delivered to the near points but the keeper has it covered. Tzolakis seems to have collided with the post and he has grabbed his head, Hull is awarded a free kick. The keeper is getting some attention but I believe he will be okay to continue.
Coventry 0-0 Hull City, 58 min: Awoniyi is almost on the end of a cross but he can’t quite get there. Both clubs are having better chances in this second half, it’s breaking up.
Everton fans threatened to “riot” if the club cash in on teenage winger Harrison Armstrong. The England Under-19s international was reportedly the subject of a £40m offer from Premier League rivals Nottingham Forest ahead of Saturday afternoon’s game away to Bournemouth.
The 19-year-old academy graduate started for the Toffees at the Vitality Stadium to make his 24th appearance for the club. Travelling supporters made their feelings clear on the situation, repeatedly chanting to the tune of Achy Breaky Heart: “Don’t sell Armstrong, Harrison Armstrong, I just don’t think you understand. If you sell Armstrong, Harrison Armstrong, you’re going to have a riot on your hands.” PA
Coventry 0-0 Hull City, 54 min: Hull have a better spell of play with multiple passes but Belloumi loses out in the box, such a disappointment after such promising build-up play.
Bournemouth 1-0 Everton, 54 min: Everton continue to toil to try and get back into this one on the scoreboard. On the balance of play they are very much competing well.
Coventry 0-0 Hull City, 51 min: Hull are growing here as Mendy takes a shot from 35 yards out and it’s another amazing bit of goalkeeping with Rushworth controlling.
Bournemouth 1-0 Everton, 50 min: Well Everton should have equalised there. Armstrong passed to Barry in the area and it took yet another fantastic Petrovic save to keep them out. What a shift the keeper is putting in.
summary: Bournemouth and Everton played to a 1-1 draw after Everton scored a late injury-time equalizer to cancel out Alex Scott's first-half goal. Meanwhile, Hull City secured a 1-0 victory over Coventry City thanks to a late winner from Liam Millar. The results leave Hull with a perfect start to the season, while Coventry continues to struggle without a goal.
key_points: Bournemouth conceded a late equalizer against Everton, resulting in a 1-1 draw after Alex Scott's earlier goal.
Hull City defeated Coventry City 1-0 with a late goal from Liam Millar, continuing their perfect start to the season.
Hull sits second in the Premier League table after winning their first two matches without conceding a goal.
Coventry fans left early as their team remained winless and goalless after two matches.
Everton fans chanted against selling teenage winger Harrison Armstrong amid reported interest from Nottingham Forest.

title: Liverpool v Nottingham Forest: How the players rated
author: Aadam Patel
content:
![Morgan Gibbs-White](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/983/cpsprodpb/9324/live/09c7f330-a3ab-11f1-af36-fffc938dca63.jpg)
- Published
Liverpool
Alisson: Well beaten for Dan Ndoye's goal but made a superb save to deny Igor Jesus on the brink of half-time and keep Liverpool in the game. Poor penalty to give away for Gibbs-White's goal. 5
Jeremie Frimpong: Struggled defensively but got into some good positions going forward. Did really well in the build-up to Florian Wirtz's disallowed goal but was just offside. Has to improve consistency with his end delivery. 6
Jeremy Jacquet: Made a goal-saving challenge to deny Igor Jesus an early goal and was impressive but still had a few moments where he was slack and lacked discipline. 6
Virgil van Dijk: Will be furious with how easily the Liverpool backline was cut open for Ndoye's opener and the ease with which Forest won their penalty. 6
Milos Kerkez: A poor display from the Liverpool left-back and was sloppy in possession. Replaced by Kostas Tsimikas in the 71st minute. 5
Dominik Szoboszlai: Solid as usual and was much more alert defensively, compared to his display at Newcastle. 6
Alexis Mac Allister: Back in the starting XI and played a lovely reverse ball for Cody Gakpo early on. Couldn't cope physically with Igor Jesus in the build up to Ndoye's goal. 6
Cody Gakpo: Started down the right in what was potentially his last Liverpool appearance and was effective. Played a lovely ball for Wirtz, then did really well to create a chance for Victor Munoz. Didn't do his defensive duties for Forest's opener but did brilliantly to create Alexander Isak's equaliser. 7
Florian Wirtz: Constantly posed a threat and unlucky not to score, having had a neat finish ruled out as Frimpong was offside and a solid header tipped over by Matz Sels. Got the assist for Munoz's goal. 7
Victor Munoz: Made his first Liverpool start and it was down his preferred left flank. The Spaniard was direct and had a penalty shout turned down but he should have tested Sels at least when he fired a first-half effort wide from inside the box. Scored a belter to level the game in front of the Kop and rescue a point for Liverpool. 7
Alexander Isak: Just six touches in the first half and zero shots on goal but made up for a forgettable opening 45 minutes with the first equaliser on the hour mark. That was just his ninth touch but a goal that will give him plenty of confidence. 6
Subs:
Tsimikas (on 71, Kerkez): 5
Gravenberch (on 71, Frimpong): 5
Ngumoha (on 71, Gakpo): 5
Araujo (on 77, Jacquet): 5
Nyoni (on 77, Mac Allister): 5
Subs not used: Mamardashvili, Endo, McConnell, Koumas.
Nottingham Forest
Matz Sels: Was commanding and it was his punt up the field that led to Ndoye's goal. Made a great save to deny Wirtz but was well-beaten by Gakpo's cross for Isak's leveller and had no chance with Munoz's strike. 5
Jair Cunha: Strong performance but will know he should have done better for Isak's goal. 6
Nikola Milenkovic: Part of a Forest backline that initially made it incredibly hard for Liverpool to break them down. 6
Murillo: Unafraid to drive with the ball and put in a solid shift but was well beaten by Munoz for the goal that made it 2-2. Still crucial that Forest keep him. 6
Ola Aina: Relentless all game. Was very involved, as always, and constantly asked questions of Liverpool. Nearly created a goal for Forest. 7
James McAtee: Getting his chance after Elliot Anderson's move to Manchester City and was very tidy on the ball in an impressive performance. Made some really good deliveries in the first half and battled well all afternoon. 7
Xaver Schlager: The summer signing came in for the injured Ibrahim Sangare and bar getting nutmegged early on by Dominik Szoboszlai, this was a good display from the Austrian midfielder. 7
Neco Williams: Like Aina, was full of energy down the opposite flank. Made a superb tackle early on to deny Gakpo. Was once on the Anfield books, and it was interesting to hear Steven Gerrard say pre-match that Liverpool should have kept him. Had a few defensive lapses but ultimately won the penalty that put Forest ahead for the second time. 7
Dan Ndoye: A wonderful finish past Alisson in the first half for what was his first Premier League goal in 377 days. 7
Morgan Gibbs-White: Quality on the ball and got the assist for Ndoye before dispatching his second-half penalty in style. Loves Anfield and now has five goal involvements (three goals, two assists) there. No Englishman has netted more Premier League goals overall this calendar year than his 13. 8
Igor Jesus: Had a great chance early on and his hold up play was brilliant for Ndoye's goal. Caused a nuisance for Liverpool's centre-backs all afternoon. 7
Subs:
Delap (on 66, Ndoye): 6
Netz (on 86, Aina): 5
Hudson-Odoi (on 90+2, McAtee): 5
Dominguez (on 90+2, Igor Jesus): 5
Subs not used: Victor, Diomande, Wood, Yates, Abbott.

summary: Liverpool secured a point in a match against Nottingham Forest thanks to goals from Alexander Isak and Victor Munoz. Dan Ndoye and Morgan Gibbs-White scored for Nottingham Forest, with Gibbs-White also providing an assist. Player ratings highlighted impactful performances from attacking players on both sides alongside defensive struggles.
key_points: Dan Ndoye scored his first Premier League goal in 377 days to open the scoring for Nottingham Forest.
Morgan Gibbs-White contributed a goal and an assist for Forest, earning an 8 rating.
Victor Munoz scored a crucial second-half equalizer for Liverpool to rescue a point.

title: Bradley Barcola: Liverpool agree Â£123m deal for PSG forward
author: Sami Mokbel; Aadam Patel
content:
![PSG's Bradley Barcola looks on before a Champions League game against Newcastle](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1024/cpsprodpb/ed0b/live/9b8840f0-a382-11f1-aac6-658882dcd3a7.jpg)
Bradley Barcola joined PSG from Lyon for Â£38.5m in 2023
- Published
Liverpool have agreed a deal worth up to Â£123m for Paris St-Germain forward Bradley Barcola.
PSG initially valued the France attacker at Â£145m, but the Reds have agreed a package worth an initial Â£106m with Â£17m in potential add-ons.
The 23-year-old is expected to have a medical this weekend before signing a long-term contract at Anfield.
Right-footed Barcola prefers to play on the left wing and his impending arrival will increase the doubts around Cody Gakpo's future at Liverpool.
Multiple sources have told BBC Sport both Tottenham Hotspur and Manchester City have shown interest in the Netherlands forward.
Liverpool are also in the market for a right winger, having explored moves for Brighton's Yankuba Minteh and Crystal Palace's Ismaila Sarr.
Barcola has become a main target for Liverpool as they look to bolster their attack following the departures of Luis Diaz and Mohamed Salah in the past two summers.
He moved to PSG from Lyon in 2023 for a reported Â£38.5m and has won three Ligue 1 titles, two Champions Leagues, the French Cup twice, as well as the Uefa Super Cup and the Fifa Intercontinental Cup.
Barcola, who scored three goals for France in this summer's World Cup, can also play on the right or through the middle and could provide cover for Alexander Isak while Hugo Ekitike recovers from a serious Achilles injury.
Speaking before Saturday's game against Nottingham Forest (12:30 BST), Reds boss Andoni Iraola was asked about Gakpo's future and said he "cannot guarantee anything", but wants to keep the 27-year-old at the club.
"[Gakpo] has been very good since he came back from the World Cup and his holiday, with a very good attitude. I hope we can keep him at that level because I think he has been very influential in our games," Iraola he said.
Analysis: Deal makes sense for both teams
Barcola has been a priority for Liverpool since Yan Diomande opted to join Real Madrid earlier in the window. The Frenchman's move to Anfield - for up to Â£123m - would be a record fee for a player leaving Ligue 1.
Barcola will bring star factor and inject real quality into a Liverpool attack that could become feared if last summer's expensive signings Isak and Florian Wirtz can step up.
PSG can feasibly look at the deal as an excellent outcome, given they signed Barcola for Â£38m and will more than triple their money - if add-ons are met - for a player who is entering the last two years of his contract and has shown no willingness to sign an extension.
Barcola was often behind Desire Doue and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia on the wings in the biggest games last season and PSG have added to their options in those areas this summer by signing Maghnes Akliouche and Mika Godts.
However Liverpool will be pleased with the deal too, having held firm earlier in the summer in terms of meeting PSG's valuation of Â£145m - but eventually bringing in one of Europe's most exciting forwards.
Why does Bradley Barcola wear number 29?
summary: Liverpool have agreed a deal worth up to £123m with Paris St-Germain for forward Bradley Barcola. The 23-year-old France international is expected to undergo a medical this weekend ahead of signing a long-term contract at Anfield. The transfer fee consists of an initial £106m with £17m in potential add-ons, setting a record for a player leaving Ligue 1.
key_points: Liverpool agreed a package worth up to £123m for PSG forward Bradley Barcola.
Barcola is expected to have a medical this weekend before signing a long-term contract.
The deal comprises an initial £106m plus £17m in potential add-ons.
Barcola's arrival adds to doubts regarding Cody Gakpo's future at the club amid interest from Tottenham and Manchester City.
PSG more than triples their money on the player they signed from Lyon for £38.5m in 2023.

title: Crystal Palace 1-4 Man City: Rayan Cherki and Erling Haaland net doubles as Enzo Maresca's reign begins with back-to-back wins
author: William Bitibiri
content:
Crystal Palace 1-4 Man City: Rayan Cherki and Erling Haaland net doubles as Enzo Maresca's reign begins with back-to-back wins
Report and free match highlights as Rayan Cherki and Erling Haaland net doubles to seal Enzo Maresca a second straight victory as Manchester City boss; Crystal Palace fall to second consecutive defeat under new boss Pierre Sage
Saturday 29 August 2026 00:31, UK
Rayan Cherki did his best Lionel Messi impression, producing moments of pure magic as Enzo Maresca's Manchester City stayed perfect in the Premier League with a 4-1 win over Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park.
First, the Frenchman, sporting the same No 10 shirt as the diminutive Argentine legend, weaved his way through the Crystal Palace defence before poking the ball past a rooted Dean Henderson to double City's lead. Erling Haaland had opened the scoring in the first half with his first goal of the season.
Despite an exciting start in Pierre Sage's first game at Selhurst Park, Haaland towered above Chris Richards to head in the opening goal.
As the applause for Cherki's opener began to fade, Yeremy Pino added to the display of individualism, beating a wall from 25 yards out and curling a free-kick that struck the bar. The ball rebounded off Gianluigi Donnarumma and therefore went down as an own goal for the Italian shotstopper.
- As it happened | Teams | Stats | Watch FREE PL highlights
- Latest news and rumours: Palace | Man City
- Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream Premier League games with no contract📺
Five minutes after his super solo effort, Cherki decided to take the sting out of Palace's newly found momentum, instantly responding to their goal with an audacious strike that deflected past Henderson.
Though Palace came close throughout, with their finest chance falling to Tyrick Mitchell, who fluffed his lines with a close-range header, Haaland's second, a rasping finish past Henderson late on, ended the contest. Palace stay in search of a first win under new boss Sage.
Maresca's City, meanwhile, made it two from two in the league, producing a dominant scoreline much more akin to what his predecessor would regularly provide.
The key moments from Selhurst Park
7: SCRAMBLE! City so close to going in front! Cherki takes a corner short and it ends up causing chaos in the Palace box.
17: GOAL! Erling Haaland leaps high above Richards to send a looping header over Henderson and into the net from Semenyo's left-wing cross.
21: BIG MISS! Should be two for City. Foden has his head in his hands as he scoops over with only the goalkeeper to beat from inside the Palace box.
28: ANOTHER FODEN MISS! How City are not further ahead, only Foden knows. He's unmarked with the goal gaping in front of him but he gets his header all wrong and Palace are able to clear the danger.
35: BIG CHANCE! What a waste from Palace! No surprise that Wharton is the creator. He's been superb. His cross from the right wing finds Mitchell in a good position but his downward header bounces wide.
54: GOAL! Cherki collects Foden's pass inside the box and jinks his way through a crowd of Palace defenders before clipping a wonderfully delicate finish beyond Henderson with the outside of his boot.
56: GOAL! It's a stunning free-kick from Pino, who curls it up and over the wall and out of reach of Donnarumma. It then crashes off the woodwork, hits the City goalkeeper in the back, and drops over the line.
59: GOAL! A third goal in five minutes, and a second for Cherki. Palace leave him in far too much space in the middle of their half and he drops a shoulder, gets himself into a shooting position, and unleashes a long-range effort which takes a deflection off Richards and whistles into the net.
84: GOAL! Haaland doubles up! Marc Guehi nips in to intercept a Richards pass and feeds Foden, who carries the ball into the box and sets up Haaland.
Cherki: I played so ****!
Man City's Rayan Cherki to Sky Sports:
"My performance was so-so.
"In the first half, we didn't find the space. I played so ****.
"When I see Enzo wants to change me, I don't like that, and I need to show them I want to play, I want to score, I want to give an assist to Erling. Today I didn't give a lot of balls to him but next time I want to give him a lot of balls."
On his first goal: "When Erling didn't get the ball, It's my instinct. I'm very happy for the win today. See you next week."
Erling Haaland interjects: "Just say what you actually mean. You scored two top goals!"
Cherki: "That is nothing. I want to give a goal for him."
Maresca: Cherki is helping us
Man City boss Enzo Maresca to Sky Sports:
On the game: "It is a tough ground. We knew it before the game. You saw it in the first few minutes of the game. But then we were in control. The intensity, the desire of the team has been very good."
On Rayan Cherki: "He's helping us. He's going to help us in the future. We know he's a quality player, last game against Bournemouth with two assists, today with two goals. But I think Rayan was very good off the ball. He was in control of Wharton and he worked very hard."
On Phil Foden: "He is adapting a little bit wide. We know he's not a winger. But we are trying to find solutions. In the last 10 or 15 minutes when he was inside, you could see he was enjoying it more. But his attitude was very good and that's what we need."
Sage angry with lack of energy from Palace subs
Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage to Sky Sports:
"I think we were able to play 60 or 65 minutes staying in the game but when I made the substitutions, the energy of the team went down, and I'm a little bit angry with that."
Angry with himself or the substitutes?: "Both. Because we are together. I will stay with my team in every moment. I talked to the players. Today, we existed in this game. We had a lot of chances. I think the 3-1 was a bad thing for us because we made the tactical mistake by not closing inside.
"They played between two players, after that they scored.
"We had a lot of chances but it's difficult to have hope against this kind of team without scoring.
"When you change players, it's about fatigue, it's about they are tired and you need more energy. I didn't find that. That's why I said to the players that we have to play as a squad and not only as a team.
"We are late in our pre-season. That's why I thought we needed to make substitutions in the moment. But you cannot replace the fatigue with less energy."
On Daniel Munoz's future: "Before the game I told you if he was with us today, it's because he is here. Same reply after."
Pundit reaction/Analysis...
Sky Sports' Jamie Redknapp at Selhurst Park:
"Cherki painted a masterpiece with that first goal. He had an amazing effect on the game. He is a genius, the things that he can do with a football. He gives you that X factor."
summary: Manchester City defeated Crystal Palace 4-1 at Selhurst Park, maintaining a perfect start to the Premier League under manager Enzo Maresca. Rayan Cherki and Erling Haaland both scored two goals each to secure the dominant victory. Palace suffered their second consecutive defeat under new boss Pierre Sage, despite a free-kick from Yeremy Pino that deflected in off Gianluigi Donnarumma.
key_points: Erling Haaland opened the scoring in the first half with a header before adding a late second goal.
Rayan Cherki scored two goals, including a solo effort through the Palace defense and a deflected long-range strike.
Yeremy Pino scored for Crystal Palace via a free-kick that hit the crossbar and deflected in off goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma.
The victory marks Manchester City's second consecutive win under new manager Enzo Maresca.

title: Crystal Palace v Man City team news: Cherki starts, Bouaddi a sub
author: Skonto Rigga
content:
Gameweek 2 of Fantasy Premier League (FPL) kicks off with a re-run of the 2025 FA Cup final: Crystal Palace v Manchester City.
Kick-off in tonight’s encounter is at 20:00 BST.
That 1-0 success at Wembley was the Eagles’ only victory over City in the last 10 attempts. The Cityzens won this fixture 3-0 both home and away last season.
This is a match that Erling Haaland loves: he’s scored in all five of his previous league meetings with the south Londoners.
Naturally, all historic records are to be taken with a pinch of salt – especially with two new managers in the dugout this season.
TEAM NEWS
It’s straightforward enough team news for City, who make the one expected alteration: Rayan Cherki in for Rico Lewis.
Nico O’Reilly likely reverts to the ‘inverted full-back’ role, with Cherki coming in as the ’10’.
Marc Guehi appears to be in central midfield again.
That’s a spot that new signing Ayyoub Bouaddi will have designs on in the medium term but for now, he’ll have to make do with a place among the substitutes.
As for Palace, head coach Pierre Sage makes four alterations from the Gameweek 1 loss at Everton.
Two are enforced as Chadi Riad and, as rumoured on Friday afternoon, Jean-Philippe Mateta miss out due to injury.
Daniel Munoz and Dwight McNeil drop to the bench.
