title: Chelsea 2-0 Luton: Danny Welbeck and Hakeem Odoffin's own goal earns Xabi Alonso a first competitive home win to reach Carabao Cup third round
author: Sam Blitz
content:
Chelsea 2-0 Luton: Danny Welbeck and Hakeem Odoffin's own goal earns Xabi Alonso a first competitive home win to reach Carabao Cup third round
Report and highlights as Chelsea beat Luton Town 2-0 in the Carabao Cup second round; Xabi Alonso named a strong Blues squad including Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Reece James; after a goalless first half, Danny Welbeck and Hakeen Odoffin's own goal saw them past Jack Wilshere's side
Thursday 27 August 2026 21:58, UK
Danny Welbeck scored on his Chelsea debut as Xabi Alonso's first competitive game at Stamford Bridge as Blues manager ended in a 2-0 win over League One Luton in the Carabao Cup second round.
With transfer news about Enzo Fernandez and Emiliano Martinez swirling through the air at Stamford Bridge before kick-off, Welbeck's 50th-minute header to open his Chelsea account showed that not all signings have to be high profile.
Alonso actually named a strong Chelsea squad for this one, with Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Reece James all starting in a bid to take the game seriously. They dominated the first half but Palmer and Estevao missed good chances, before Rogers hit the bar with the last kick of the half.
- As it happened | Teams | Stats
- Carabao Cup third round draw in full
- Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream Premier League games with no contract📺
But Welbeck broke Luton's resistance with a bullet header from Malo Gusto to open his Chelsea account in his 19th season playing in England's top league.
His achievements are so impressive that it is worth remembering that he and Luton head coach Jack Wilshere were once Arsenal team-mates.
But it was someone 16 years Welbeck's junior who sealed the result as Estevao's silky run and finish ended the contest with 10 minutes to go - though it would go down as a Hakeem Odoffin own goal.
The result sees Chelsea book a Carabao Cup third-round tie against Leeds United in early September, while Wilshere's Luton lost for the first time in 16 matches in all competitions - which was the longest run out of England's top four leagues.
The key moments from Stamford Bridge
11: DOUBLE CHANCE! Chelsea start strongly and Palmer has two quickfire efforts saved by Luton goalkeeper Josh Keeley.
19: GOOD SAVE! The Chelsea onslaught continues as James' free-kick is well-saved by Keeley.
39: WIDE! Estevao gets into a good area but drags his effort well wide of goal.
44: SAVE! Luton's best chance of the first half sees Odoffin head a free-kick at goal, but Mike Penders saves.
45+1: OFF THE BAR! Chelsea's best chance of the game sees Rogers hit the bar from Estevao's run and cross.
50: GOAL! Luton's resistance is broken as Welbeck heads home from the middle of the box after Gusto's cross.
67: CHANCE! Kasey Palmer has a good shot from distance but it flies just wide of the near post.
79: GOAL! Estevao seals the win after doing a stepover before finding the opposite corner with a slick finish, which then goes down as a Odoffin own goal.
90+2: CHANCES! Substitute Joao Pedro misses a sitter before fellow replacement Jamie Gittens strikes the foot of the post.
Alonso: We have to prepare for low blocks
Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso to Sky Sports:
"We needed to play with patience. Luton were defending with heart, they were solid so we knew that if they defend that low, it's not easy. At half-time, we spoke to be patient and keep going.
"It's the first time we have played against a low block this season, we have to prepare for when teams play in that way.
"We want to have a complete squad in all aspects. In quality, personality, young and experienced players - so the young players get help, that they are still players to develop.
"I'm happy with the energy and attitude of the players. The crowd has been great, we need them for the whole season. We come back here on Sunday."
Analysis: New formation gives Chelsea a Plan B
Sky Sports' Sam Blitz:
On Monday, there was reason for excitement about Alonso's Chelsea. The 3-4-3 formation at Fulham saw some brilliant attacking plays - but in this game we saw something a bit different.
Alonso switched it up with a 4-2-3-1 formation, putting Palmer in as the No 10 behind Welbeck - and it added a different dimension to the Chelsea attack.
Yes, the gulf in class between Chelsea and League One Luton is fairly big but the Blues' attacking players thrived. Estevao and Palmer both ended up with five chances created each - in a Chelsea attack that created 26 shots.
Many saw Alonso's time at Real Madrid and thought a back four wasn't possible. But after this dominant display, Chelsea have a different game plan they can turn to - after years of being accused of not having a Plan B.
Wilshere: We don't like losing
Luton Town head coach Jack Wilshere to Sky Sports:
"Proud is the word that comes to mind the most. We saw things in the team tonight that we don't normally have to do.
"For as long as Chelsea made us do it, I loved it. I loved how focused we were. The first goal is a really good goal that's hard to defend. And then you think can you stay in it still? Towards the end I think we got a bit tired, but really proud of the commitment and the effort.
"We don't like losing, we knew it would be difficult but I'm proud of the players. No-one in that dressing room is happy or sad - I'm proud of them. But we haven't lost in a while and we don't like that losing feeling. We want to create that winning culture and feeling."
summary: Chelsea defeated Luton Town 2-0 in the Carabao Cup second round to earn manager Xabi Alonso his first competitive home win at Stamford Bridge. Danny Welbeck opened the scoring with a header on his Chelsea debut in the 50th minute. A late goal, officially recorded as a Hakeem Odoffin own goal following Estevao's run, sealed the victory and advanced Chelsea to the third round against Leeds United.
key_points: Danny Welbeck scored on his Chelsea debut with a 50th-minute header from a Malo Gusto cross.
A second goal came with 10 minutes remaining when Estevao's run and finish resulted in a Hakeem Odoffin own goal.
Manager Xabi Alonso secured his first competitive home win since taking charge of Chelsea.
The victory advanced Chelsea to the Carabao Cup third round to face Leeds United.
Jack Wilshere's Luton side suffered their first defeat in 16 matches across all competitions.

title: Muniz and García on target in Fulham’s Carabao Cup cruise past Wimbledon
author: John Brewin
content:
Fulham’s second London derby this week, a first competitive win for Álvaro Arbeloa. If AFC Wimbledon represent a different echelon to Chelsea, Monday’s visitors, Thursday’s easy progress past League One opponents supplied several reasons for optimism in the new Fulham.
Marco Silva, Arbeloa’s predecessor, frequently offered sullen dismissal of the depth of his Fulham squad and yet left behind plenty of talent on departing for Benfica. Getting a better tune from Emile Smith Rowe and Rodrigo Muniz than Silva managed last season will help. The pair scored first-half goals to take the tie from Wimbledon’s reach, making for a second half of comfort and experimentation, glimpses of a different Fulham, teenage talent handed its chance to shine. Gonzalo García’s late strike, rounding Wimbledon goalkeeper Nathan Bishop for a second goal of the week, increased the excitement surrounding one of the summer’s most eye-catching signings.
“You need the energy and different qualities,” said Arbeloa of an evening where squad rotation had paid dividends. “They need to feel they are important.”
A muggy riverside evening attracted a decent crowd. More than enough to disrupt the dog walkers and evening strollers of a genteel locale, the Wimbledon contingent boisterous. The first meeting between the clubs since 2001, before the old Wimbledon was franchised to Milton Keynes and a phoenix club rose from that rotten affair.
The respective team selections revealed priorities; 10 changes for Arbeloa, only Oscar Bobb remained from Chelsea; six for Johnnie Jackson, the Wimbledon manager. Shea Charles, the summer’s other headline signing, made his first start and played well. “He’s ready,” said Arbeloa of the young Northern Ireland midfielder.
Luc De Fougerolles, fresh from the summer’s World Cup with Canada, made only his second Fulham appearance. Down each team’s left, a Sessegnon brother, Ryan for Fulham and Steven, formerly of Fulham, for Wimbledon.
“A good night for the club because we get to test ourselves against the very best,” said Jackson. “And 5,000 fans got to enjoy themselves. They were a credit to the club.”
Wimbledon, maintaining Crazy Gang traditions, were dangerous from set pieces. When De Fougerolles could only head away a corner, the ball fell to the Wimbledon captain, Alistair Smith. The shot was straight at Benjamin Lecomte, the best chance on offer to the visitors all evening.
Thereafter, Fulham piled up opportunities. Goals soon followed. Smith Rowe was furious after a sliced miss. Muniz was just as self-flagellating when ballooning a Smith Rowe flick.
![Gonzalo García raises his right arm in celebration as he scores](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/eac9ef3f3f82c24c9f84600a61ad839a69b61c9e/0_0_5400_3600/master/5400.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
His redemption came swiftly, from close range after Dons defender James Tilley deflected the ball into his path. The celebration was minimal from a player Arbeloa said “deserves more minutes”.
after newsletter promotion
Muniz was far more rapturous after nodding in Kenny Tete’s cross. Small wonder. This was his first goal since the opening game of last season. “Goals are very important for strikers,” said Arbeloa, stating the clear and obvious.
At half-time Macaulay Zepa, 18, arrived. Arbeloa’s appointment was accompanied by heralding of his youth development work at Real Madrid, a departure from Silva’s preference for hard-bitten pros. Zepa, a speedy and direct winger, showed real promise, as did fellow youth team graduate Chibby Nwoko. “One of the best news today,” said Arbeloa. “We know very well that academy players are very important.”
Fulham featured an assured youth-and-experience central defensive combination of De Fougerolles and Joachim Andersen. Calvin Bassey replaced the senior partner on the hour and the youngster did not last much longer, pulling up after a block tackle. “Nothing to worry about,” said Arbeloa, soothingly.
The arrivals of García and César Palacios, young Madrilenos who accompanied Arbeloa, supplied further excitement, the former’s goal another taste of a new Fulham.
summary: Fulham secured a comfortable Carabao Cup victory over AFC Wimbledon, marking Álvaro Arbeloa's first competitive win as manager. First-half goals from Emile Smith Rowe and Rodrigo Muniz put Fulham in control, before substitute Gonzalo García added a late strike. The match also provided opportunities for squad rotation and youth integration, with teenagers like Macaulay Zepa and Chibby Nwoko featuring.
key_points: Fulham defeated AFC Wimbledon in the Carabao Cup to secure Álvaro Arbeloa's first competitive win.
Emile Smith Rowe and Rodrigo Muniz scored first-half goals to secure the victory.
Gonzalo García scored a late goal to round off the win for Fulham.
Manager Álvaro Arbeloa utilized squad rotation and gave opportunities to young academy players like Macaulay Zepa.

title: Liverpool agree £120m deal for Bradley Barcola after breakthrough talks with PSG
author: Andy Hunter
content:
Liverpool are closing in on a £120m deal for Bradley Barcola after a breakthrough in talks with Paris Saint-Germain. Barcola has been Liverpool’s main transfer target all summer only for PSG’s £145m valuation to prove a significant hurdle.
However, further negotiations on Thursday night ended in an outline agreement being reached over a compromise fee. Liverpool have agreed to pay a guaranteed sum of just over £100m for the France international, with add-ons based on individual and team success, taking the overall package to about £120m.
The full structure of the deal has not been finalised, but last night’s breakthrough, coupled with PSG’s willingness to lower their asking price for the 23-year-old, should allow Barcola to complete his move before Tuesday’s transfer deadline. Liverpool were informed last month the player was keen to join them, having fallen down the pecking order at PSG.
Barcola has two years remaining on his PSG contract, but informed the club that he will not be signing an extension. The two-time European champions have added Ferran Torres, Maghnes Akliouche and Mika Godts to their formidable attacking options this summer and have omitted Barcola from their matchday squads this season.
PSG signed Barcola for €45m from Lyon in 2023 and the winger has played a prominent role in the rise of the Champions League winners. But Enrique’s preference for a front line of Désiré Doué, Ousmane Dembélé and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia in PSG’s biggest matches last season prompted Barcola to consider his options.
The arrival of Barcola – and sources insist it is not done yet – would make him the second-most expensive signing in Liverpool’s history behind the £125m Alexander Isak, but the club have still to land a replacement for Mohamed Salah on the right. Liverpool have had two bids rejected by Brighton for Yankuba Minteh and, despite enquiring over Ismaïla Sarr’s availability, have not made an offer for the Crystal Palace forward.
Cody Gakpo’s future at Liverpool will be in doubt should the club sign two wingers before the deadline. The Netherlands international has interest from Tottenham and Manchester City.
summary: Liverpool have reached an outline agreement with Paris Saint-Germain for a £120m deal to sign winger Bradley Barcola before the transfer deadline. The 23-year-old France international, who has two years left on his contract and refused to sign an extension, is keen to join Liverpool after falling down the pecking order at PSG. The transfer package consists of a guaranteed sum over £100m plus add-ons, pending the finalization of the deal's structure.
key_points: Liverpool and PSG agreed on a compromise fee of about £120m for Bradley Barcola.
Barcola informed PSG he would not sign a contract extension and is keen to join Liverpool.
PSG lowered their initial £145m asking price following Thursday night negotiations.
The 23-year-old winger has been omitted from PSG matchday squads this season.

title: Preston North End 0-4 Everton: Thierno Barry scores hat-trick as David Moyes' Toffees saunter into Carabao Cup third round
author: Dan Long
content:
Preston North End 0-4 Everton: Thierno Barry scores hat-trick as David Moyes' Toffees saunter into Carabao Cup third round
Report and free match highlights from the Carabao Cup second-round tie between Preston North End and Everton at Deepdale; Thierno Barry follows up his goal in the Premier League opener with a hat-trick and an assist to send the Toffees into third round
Wednesday 26 August 2026 23:25, UK
Thierno Barry scored three goals and set up the other as Everton sauntered into the third round of the Carabao Cup by way of a 4-0 win over Preston at Deepdale.
The French striker scored eight goals in 41 games in 2025/26 and, after his first of the season in Saturday's Premier League win over Crystal Palace, is now already halfway to matching that total despite having played 38 games fewer.
The Toffees - who have not progressed past the third round since 2023/24 - have been drawn to face Wolves in the next round.

A strong Everton team were in control from the off. They dominated the ball and chances came thick and fast against a Preston side who've lost two from two in the Sky Bet Championship but, for the most part, those openings were of low quality.
The 10th attempt was a successful one. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall's floated ball released Vitalii Mykolenko on the left, who laid the ball on a plate for Barry to sweep in a tidy finish.
There was a feeling the floodgates might open after that, but they didn't, so when the second half began, Preston had the bit between their teeth, which the crowd sensed.
However, Barry's second just before the hour made the comeback less likely, and his simple finish to complete his hat-trick essentially secured Everton's progression with 20 minutes to play.
There was time for Brennan Johnson to add shine to the result, with the Welshman - who joined from Crystal Palace earlier this month - netting his first goal since November 2025 to make it 4-0.
- 25: GOAL! After nine previous attempts, Barry finishes off a slick move to put Everton in front.
- 39: CHANCE! Merlin Rohl gifts Preston a chance when he misjudges a bounce, allowing Delano Burgzorg to pull the ball back to Leo Leroy, who fires over from a promising position.
- 45: SAVE! Great stop from North End debutant Lee Nicholls, who denies Tyler Dibling at his near post.
- 47: BLOCK! James Tarkowski sticks a foot in to brilliantly turn away Delano Burgzorg's shot as Preston chase an equaliser.
- 59: GOAL! Iliman Ndiaye tees up Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, whose cross is pushed straight into the path of Barry, who makes no mistake.
- 65: SAVE! Jordan Pickford makes his only significant save of the night to keep out a sweetly-struck overhead kick from Callum Lang.
- 70: GOAL! Dewsbury-Hall finds substitute Johnson, who gains a yard on Lewis Gibson and squares for Barry, who sweeps in to complete his hat-trick.
- 72: GOAL! Barry turns provider, laying a beautiful ball off for Johnson, who arrives in a similar position, but this time goes alone to add the gloss.
Heckingbottom: The second goal changed the game
Preston's Paul Heckingbottom speaking on Sky Sports Football:
"It's just frustrating we were going to make the subs and they scored the (second) goal as we had them all lined up. It just changed the game. The goals after that were disappointing
"We were playing against top opposition, we know that, but one or two things, fundamentally, don't help you keep clean sheets anyway. It doesn't matter who you are playing against.
"Because of where we are at the minute, it's hard to take the pressure off the defenders as we've not got attacking changes. We've got defenders on the bench, a couple more midfielders, wing-backs and some young boys. That's where we're at; we need attacking changes so we can keep the pressure on. And that's a problem for us at the minute."
Moyes discusses progression, Barry and Johnson
Everton's David Moyes speaking on Sky Sports Football:
"It ended up being a little bit more comfortable than I thought it might have been before the game, but it's a really good result for us.
"I thought we played well at times and our football was quite good, but we need to finish things off a bit better in the first half than we did, but I'm really pleased we scored four goals."
On Thierno Barry: "I told him [at the end of last season] he has to do a lot better than he did before. That's it. We want centre-forwards to score goals. I don't think it's easy for anybody coming to the Premier League in their first season, especially centre-forwards. He'll learn a lot more, he'll see a lot more and he's come in with a much better attitude generally, so whoever's working with him is doing a good job."
On Brennan Johnson: "We want to find what he did at Tottenham when he was scoring all those goals. His assist tonight was brilliant and his finish as well. People who've watched Brennan over the years will tell you that looks a bit more like him. We don't want to bring him on too quick, but he's done well tonight."
summary: Everton advanced to the Carabao Cup third round with a comfortable 4-0 victory over Preston North End at Deepdale. French striker Thierno Barry starred in the match by scoring a hat-trick and providing an assist. Summer signing Brennan Johnson also added a goal for David Moyes' side, securing a matchup against Wolves in the next round.
key_points: Thierno Barry scored a hat-trick and registered an assist in Everton's 4-0 win.
Brennan Johnson netted his first goal since November 2025 to round out the scoring.
Everton advanced past the Carabao Cup second round and will face Wolves in the third round.
Preston struggled to create high-quality chances and remain winless across their early fixtures.

Everton have been involved in every EFL Cup third-round draw since 2002, and they should have too much quality for their second-round opponents Preston, who have got off to a slow start in their Championship campaign.
Several Premier League clubs seemed ill-prepared for their opening matches, but Everton showed their readiness by overcoming Crystal Palace in an entertaining encounter.
Moyes's men had a few scares against the Eagles, who wasted a couple of glorious chances to take a first-half lead, but they grew into the game and never looked back from the moment Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall broke the deadlock with a sumptuous strike.
Dewsbury-Hall could be among the players given a midweek breather as Moyes keeps an eye on Saturday's Premier League trip to Bournemouth, but the Scot will be equally aware of the Everton fans' desire for their team to have a good run in the cup competitions and is sure to select an experienced starting line-up with plenty of talent on the bench.

title: Uefa poised to lift boycott threat after Fifa promises no World Cup sale repeat
author: Nick Ames; Matt Hughes
content:
Uefa is poised to drop its threatened boycott of Fifa competitions after receiving concrete guarantees that the global governing body will never attempt a repeat of Gianni Infantino’s plan to sell stakes in the World Cup.
The Guardian understands European teams are likely to be cleared for participation in the upcoming Under-20 Women’s World Cup, along with subsequent tournaments, after Fifa provided the binding assurances that no equivalent of its president’s ill-fated scheme will be put on the table.
Uefa had threatened the boycott after Infantino’s Fifa Forward Enterprise proposal was revealed and doubled down after it was withdrawn, saying the condition that “such attempts to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again” had not been met.
Quick Guide
How do I sign up for sport breaking news alerts?
In the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.
If you already have the Guardian app, make sure you’re on the most recent version.
If you don't have the Guardian app, download it from the iOS App Store on iPhone or the Google Play store on Android by searching for 'The Guardian'.
Despite exchanging barbs in public, Uefa and Fifa are understood to have been having private discussions over the terms of removing the boycott threat for several weeks with the European governing body finally getting the reassurances it required.
When Fifa confirmed its decision to abandon FFE four days after it became public it neglected to pledge that a similar privatisation plan would not be repeated, but it has now done so in private correspondence.
A decision to drop the boycott will allow England, who named their squad for the under-20 tournament last week, to travel to Poland in time for the opening game against Canada on 5 September.
![England’s under-20s pose before a friendly this month in Portugal.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/32dcf1521121fbea340b7cf0a45d904e80da8c61/430_474_4563_2676/master/4563.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
France and Spain had also listed their travelling party in anticipation that the boycott would be lifted. Portugal, Italy and the host nation are the other European countries due to compete.
While the boycott is yet to be publicly dropped, it is among the topics that may arise in a meeting of Uefa’s executive committee and federation chiefs in Monte Carlo on Thursday. The 55 heads of Uefa’s member associations will convene before the Champions League draw during what is traditionally a significant few days in the European football calendar.
after newsletter promotion
Uefa’s position that Infantino must be replaced has not changed and further steps regarding its stance towards the Fifa leadership will also be discussed at the meeting. Italy’s football federation (FIGC) on Wednesday became the latest to publicly withdraw support for Infantino. “This decision is intended to clearly and transparently express the FIGC’s position ... regarding the recent initiatives promoted by the Fifa president concerning the governance and development of international competitions,” it said.
There will be relief in some quarters that younger players, in particular, will not become embroiled in the volatile battle for football’s future. But the fact that Fifa has been forced to mitigate for its president’s actions is another humiliation for a persistently scandal-hit organisation.
summary: Uefa is expected to drop its threatened boycott of Fifa competitions after receiving binding assurances that Fifa will never repeat Gianni Infantino's plan to sell stakes in the World Cup. The resolution follows weeks of private discussions and will clear European teams to participate in upcoming tournaments, including the Under-20 Women's World Cup. However, Uefa's stance that Infantino must be replaced remains unchanged, with further discussions regarding Fifa leadership expected at an upcoming meeting.
key_points: Uefa is poised to lift its boycott threat against Fifa after receiving concrete guarantees regarding World Cup stake sales.
The assurances clear the way for European teams, including England, to compete in the Under-20 Women's World Cup in Poland.
Despite resolving the boycott issue, Uefa's position that Fifa president Gianni Infantino must be replaced remains unchanged.
Italy's football federation recently joined others in publicly withdrawing support for Infantino.

title: Ayyoub Bouaddi: Manchester City sign Morocco midfielder from Lille in Â£86m deal
author: Paul Battison; Shamoon Hafez
content:
![Ayyoub Bouaddi in a Manchester City tracksuit top holding a pen with a contract on the desk in front of him](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1056/cpsprodpb/f8b4/live/8c35e240-a13b-11f1-9311-09d4e1fc9016.jpg)
Ayyoub Bouaddi has won eight caps for Morocco
- Published
Manchester City have signed midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille in a Â£85.6m deal to make the Morocco international the Premier League's most expensive teenager.
The 18-year-old joins on a five-year contract, subject to international clearance, with City paying Â£81.4m upfront plus Â£4.2m in add-ons.
Enzo Maresca's side moved to sign Bouaddi after selling central midfielders Rodri to Barcelona in a Â£65m deal and Tijjani Reinders to Al-Qadsiah for Â£52m.
He impressed at this summer's World Cup - starting five of Morocco's six matches in their run to the quarter-finals - after becoming a key member of Lille's side in Ligue 1.
"This is a very special day for me and my family. Manchester City are, for me, the best club in the world. It's a dream to be here and be able to call myself a City player," said Bouaddi.
"I have spent most of my life working hard to become the best player I can be and reach the top of the game.
"I've watched City for many years, and I love their style of play. City always try and play quality football. And they have shown they are winners - this club feels like it's built to win."
The fee for Bouaddi surpasses the Â£58.9m paid by Manchester United to sign French defender Leny Yoro, also from Lille, in 2024.
Bouaddi made 96 appearances for Lille after making his debut in 2023, helping them finish third in Ligue 1 last season.
At the age of 16 he became the youngest footballer to ever play for the French side on his senior debut against Faroese club KI in the Europa League, before announcing himself on the world stage by playing a starring role in Lille's Champions League victory over Real Madrid in 2024.
Bouaddi will form part of a revamped midfield, with City already bringing in England midfielder Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for Â£116m.
Bouaddi functions as a deep-lying conductor and would complement Anderson, who is comfortable as a box-to-box midfielder as well as the number six role he plays for England.
City are also set to make an offer for Chelsea's Argentina midfielder Enzo Fernandez but it remains to be seen whether a deal can be struck with the 25-year-old valued at Â£120m.
Bouaddi's signing comes after Brazilian winger Savinho, now known as Savio, joined Tottenham in a Â£75m deal earlier this week.
Spurs have also agreed a loan deal to sign City's Egypt forward Omar Marmoush, while Spain midfielder Nico Gonzalez is set to leave Maresca's side to join Newcastle in a Â£52m deal.
Analysis - Midfield rebuild taking shape
City's midfield transformation continues to take shape with the acquisition of teenage star Bouaddi, who will play alongside club-record signing Anderson.
At just 18, Bouaddi has big boots to fill following the departure of 2024 Ballon d'Or winner Rodri, who became one of the best midfielders in the world at City and departed for Barcelona last week.
But with Bouaddi, they are paying for a player with undoubted potential rather than being the finished product, which heaps plenty of pressure on his young shoulders.
Rodri, Reijnders and Bernardo Silva have all left from City's midfield this summer and Nico Gonzalez is also set to make an exit after Newcastle agreed a Â£52m deal for the player.
It means Maresca still needs reinforcements in the middle of the park and City will make an offer for Chelsea's Â£120m-rated midfielder Enzo Fernandez to bolster ranks - whether they can match the asking price and get the deal done before Tuesday's deadline remains to be seen.
There has been significant change in the City squad this summer and with the season already under way Anderson, Bouaddi and possibly Fernandez will all need to hit the ground running.
summary: Manchester City have signed Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille on a five-year contract in an £85.6m deal, making him the Premier League's most expensive teenager. The 18-year-old arrives following the departures of midfielders like Rodri and Tijjani Reijnders. Bouaddi made 96 appearances for Lille and impressed during Morocco's run to the World Cup quarter-finals.
key_points: Ayyoub Bouaddi joined Manchester City from Lille for £85.6m (£81.4m upfront plus £4.2m add-ons) on a five-year deal.
The fee makes the 18-year-old the Premier League's most expensive teenager, surpassing Leny Yoro's £58.9m move to Manchester United.
Bouaddi started five of Morocco's six matches during their run to the World Cup quarter-finals.
His signing comes as part of a midfield rebuild under Enzo Maresca following the exits of players such as Rodri and Tijjani Reijnders.

title: Celtic deficiencies laid bare at LASK on another night of Champions League pain
author: Tom English
content:
![Celtic captain Callum McGregor looks dejected](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/1fce/live/e1442240-a115-11f1-92eb-a9b3bbcf6f4a.jpg)
After throwing away a 4-0 aggregate lead, Celtic will now compete in the Europa League
- Published
When Callum McGregor eviscerated his own team-mates in the wake of Celtic's stupefying Champions League collapse against LASK, he delivered their one coherent moment of a spineless night.
In branding his fellow players "passive" and "scared" and in then sending a telling shot across their bows - "now we'll see what people are made of" - it is hard to recall him being so full of fury after a European game.
And there are plenty to choose from, plenty of dark nights, plenty of embarrassment, plenty of soul-searching over many years.
For close to a decade he has been Celtic's best player, a near ever-present. That longevity has brought him many trophies, but he's been around for many mortifications, too.
Where losing a 4-0 advantage ranks in the pantheon of Celtic failures is a moot point. What is unarguable is that it was a total capitulation, a feeble collapse in the face of LASK's physicality and desire and belief.
The Celtic captain called his players "scared" when winning 4-0. No media hatchet man could come up with a more damaging word to describe what happened out there.
McGregor has been through the European mill.
He was there last season when Celtic's fecklessness saw them go goalless for 210 minutes against the popgun boys of Kairat Almaty before failing to score from three of their five penalties in the shootout.
He was there for the 7-1 against Borussia Dortmund and the 6-0 against Atletico Madrid.
He's a survivor of the Champions League play-off exit to Midtjylland and the pair of 4-1 losses to Sparta Prague in the Europa League.
He was around for earlier Champions League play-off exits against Ferencvaros, AEK Athens and Cluj.
He's a veteran of the 7-1 loss to PSG and the 7-0 loss to Barcelona. He wears the scars as much as he holds the medals.
It is difficult, though, to recall him being as seething as he was on Tuesday night.
He wasn't ranting - that is not his style. He spoke calmly which lent his words more power.
He was raging in his own way. Raging at another exit, raging that when the chips were down too many of his fellow players panicked and allowed themselves to be overrun, raging at professional pride being trampled underfoot for all to see.
'Rabbits in headlights don't look as lost as Celtic did'
'We're a million miles from the finished article' - O'Neill after Celtic's Champions League exit
It was McGregor who opened the scoring on the night, a deflected shot and a 4-0 lead on aggregate.
LASK had started well but that goal looked to all the world like a kick to their solar plexus. They had chances in Glasgow and they had chances in the opening minutes in Linz - and they were 4-0 down!
How many punches can one team take before they lose their fight? Many, as it turned out.
Celtic were obliging, of course. Painfully so. We trumpeted their classy goals and their adventurous play a week ago and wrongly assumed that they had gumption to go with it. Big mistake.
When Benjamin Nygren's ridiculously loose pass led directly to LASK's equaliser on the night, the first signs of a wobble were visible.
Thirty two minutes had been played and Celtic did not look wholly comfortable at 4-1 on aggregate. Mad, but true.
When they conceded again three minutes into the second half, there were a few jelly legs on show. Auston Trusty was culpable this time. Brushed off the ball. Swatted and 4-2 now.
Trusty was poor, not the only one, but a point of real weakness that LASK went for.
Ten minutes after the hosts scored their second, they scored their third. Too many parts of the Celtic team were in full fright mode now. The slow death was picking up pace.
Camilo Duran, the hero of the first leg, was reduced to a non-event. Kasper Hogh worked hard but with no impact. Passes went astray. Celtic were directionless. Everything fell apart.
Rabbits in headlights do not tend to look as lost as Celtic did when the pressure really hit.
If McGregor was trying to put out fires in his own team he was failing. He could not cut through the tension.
Martin O'Neill looked on like a man 10 years older than his true age. This was a shocking night for him. One of his worst in football, he said later. He took responsibility, but he cannot be alone in that.
He emptied his bench in a desperate attempt to stem the flow, but his substitutions, five in 12 befuddled minutes, had zero impact.
Celtic did not have a shot on target in the second half of normal time nor in extra-time. They only existed as a man hanging off a cliff edge exists. There was only one way this was going to end.
LASK's fourth goal might have come in the 90th minute but it was deserved.
By that point they'd had 33 shots on Celtic's goal (they finished on 40) to go with the 20 from last week. It was a rout.
Cameron Carter-Vickers was hobbling about on one leg. Hogh much the same. Forward came the waves and Celtic tried to hold them back with a back four of Anthony Ralston, Dane Murray, Trusty and Liam Scales.
The fifth goal was a mercy, and another Celtic player doing the wrong thing at the wrong time in the wrong place. For Nygren and Trusty read Luke McCowan. Hapless and helpless - and out of the Champions League.
'Celtic ambition will be questioned again'
The night meandered to its conclusion. LASK missed a penalty for 6-1 before Miguel Freckleton, recently of St Mirren, slalomed his way into the Celtic box and threatened, for a second, to score.
All credit to Freckleton and his new beginning in Austria, but in flashes he was made to look like a serious player in his few minutes on the pitch. When that kind of thing happens it tells a story.
Celtic were beyond disarray by then. Spooked, over-powered, out-fought, out-played. The smooth-running killers of last week in Glasgow was an optical illusion that hid psychological deficiencies.
Nobody could have predicted that they would fall in such a heap at 4-0, but they did.
Celtic, quite obviously, need a back-up left-back to Kieran Tierney and they don't have one.
They absolutely need, and this is no secret, a physical presence in the middle of the pitch, a player of stature in every sense of the word, a guy who would not be bullied as Celtic were bullied in Austria. They don't have one of those either.
They have done good deals but not enough of them. They're in net profit in their transfer business this summer.
The A-word - ambition - is going to get another airing. When you finish a Â£40m match with a back four of Ralston, Murray, Trusty and Scales then, as a club, you have not done your work properly. Nobody did on the night, on the field and off.
All those other defeats were incredibly costly in a financial but also in a self-worth sense.
They hoped they'd left the Champions League drawing board behind, but they're right back where they were when Kairat and Midtjylland and Ferencvaros and Cluj and AEK were the ones inflicting the pain.
Incredibly, another name has to get added to the list.
summary: Celtic suffered a disastrous Champions League collapse, surrendering a 4-0 aggregate lead to lose against LASK and drop into the Europa League. Captain Callum McGregor harshly criticized his teammates after the match, describing them as scared and passive during the heavy defeat. The team's lack of physical presence, squad depth, and defensive stability were brutally exposed as LASK dominated the match with 40 shots on goal.
key_points: Celtic blew a 4-0 aggregate lead against LASK, resulting in a dramatic Champions League exit.
Captain Callum McGregor slammed his teammates as passive and scared following the defeat.
LASK recorded 40 shots on goal over the course of the match, overpowering a depleted and struggling Celtic side.
The loss highlighted Celtic's squad deficiencies, including a lack of physical presence in midfield and defensive depth.

title: Martin O’Neill puts Champions League collapse among most painful Celtic nights
author: Guardian sport
content:
Martin O’Neill has admitted that Celtic’s Champions League qualifying collapse from 4-0 up ranks as one of his most painful nights as the club’s manager.
Celtic held a four-goal aggregate lead against Lask on Tuesday when Callum McGregor scored in the 21st minute in Austria, building on a 3-0 first-leg victory, and appeared to be cruising into the league stage. But they lost 5-1 on the night after extra time to go out in extraordinary fashion.
Defeat sends Celtic into the Europa League and delivers a damaging financial blow that will cost the club at least £20m. O’Neill, who has overseen more than 300 games as the club’s manager, said the loss on Tuesday was one of the most painful.
“I would say absolutely, yes,” the 74-year-old said. “I’d put it down before the disappointment of losing the Uefa Cup final in 2003, but it’s so, so disappointing.
“We should have been out of sight by half-time. We scored a goal, which was great, we missed two great, great opportunities. And then we give them a lifeline just before half-time and then one just after it. And they come roaring back. And obviously we conceded, from our viewpoint, not good goals at all. But that’s my team and that’s my responsibility.”
Asked whether his squad was strong enough, O’Neill said: “These are tough games. And it might only be a Champions League qualifying game, but it felt like a Champions League game. I thought they were a fine side. But that doesn’t matter. We should have been able to have seen it through. And we didn’t do. Talking about the squad, that’s for another day.”
Quick Guide
Play our football trivia game, On the ball
McGregor, the captain, accepted there were no excuses. “We got what we deserved,” he told Amazon Prime. “I thought we were so passive. All night. We actually looked scared to go and win the game, and when you are 3-0 up it’s psychological.
“To be honest I didn’t think we were that good in the first leg, either. We scored at good times and kind of got away with it. You go 3-0 and you think you’ve got a real chance but when you play like that you can’t have any excuse whatsoever.
“We have to suck it up, apologise to the supporters and the club because there is no way that we should lose that game … Now you’ll see what kind of characters are in there.”
summary: Celtic manager Martin O'Neill described the team's Champions League qualifying collapse against Lask as one of the most painful nights of his career. After holding a 4-0 aggregate lead, Celtic lost 5-1 on the night after extra time, missing out on the league stage. The defeat relegates the club to the Europa League and results in an estimated financial loss of at least £20m.
key_points: Celtic blew a four-aggregate-goal lead to lose 5-1 on the night against Lask in a Champions League qualifier.
Manager Martin O'Neill ranked the defeat among the most painful nights of his managerial tenure.
The elimination costs the club at least £20m in a damaging financial blow and sends them to the Europa League.
Captain Callum McGregor admitted the team played passively and offered no excuses for the collapse.

title: Manchester City confirm Bouaddi signing as Marmoush and González head out
author: Jamie Jackson; David Hytner
content:
Manchester City have confirmed the signing of Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille for €95m (£81.4m) plus €5m, with the 18-year-old midfielder agreeing a five-year contract.
Bouaddi’s arrival comes after City struck deals to loan Omar Marmoush to Tottenham for the season, with an obligation to buy for an initial £50m, and sell Nico González to Newcastle for £52m.
Bouaddi has experienced a rapid rise after becoming Lille’s youngest player when featuring against KÍ Klaksvík on 5 October 2023, three days after his 16th birthday. The Morocco international played 96 times for Lille and becomes the most expensive teenager signed by an English club.
Quick Guide
Play our football trivia game, On the ball
He said: “I am happy with the progress I have made so far, but I also know I can improve so much. This is undoubtedly the best place for me to do that. This club demands trophies and I will give everything to make sure we are challenging for every title.”
Hugo Viana, City’s director of football, said: “Ayyoub’s potential is extremely high – a player equipped with everything a top midfielder needs. At just 18, he already has outstanding football intelligence and that will only improve under the guidance of Enzo [Maresca].”
Bouaddi, who has played mainly as a No 6, continues City’s midfield rebuild. González is poised to become the fourth frontline central midfielder to depart this summer, after Rodri, Bernardo Silva and Tijjani Reijnders. City have added Bouaddi and Elliott Anderson, a £116m buy from Nottingham Forest, and are expected to firm up their interest in Chelsea’s Enzo Fernández by making a bid. The west London club value the midfielder at £120m.
Marmoush is to have a medical at Spurs, who have agreed to pay up to £10m in add-ons, with half of that guaranteed. Next summer the 27-year-old is to sign a four-year contract with a one-year option.
![Omar Marmoush pictured during a Manchester City game](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/1604a438847b7263e4df312f2ac37c79e462d09e/41_98_4071_2645/master/4071.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
City are not due to give a sell-on fee to Eintracht Frankfurt, from whom they bought the Egyptian in January 2025. Marmoush is following Sávio in leaving City for Spurs, who bought the Brazilian winger in a £75m plus £10m deal on Tuesday. City have agreed a £34m fee for Palmeiras’s Allan Elias, who is to be Sávio’s replacement as a wide forward.
after newsletter promotion
The Spurs manager, Roberto De Zerbi, has been keen to bolster his options at centre-forward and Marmoush represents an upgrade on Dominic Solanke and Richarlison, who have struggled for consistency and fitness.
De Zerbi said at the end of July that Spurs had a “bomba” attacking signing lined up, meaning a top-tier player, and Marmoush and Sávio fit the bill. They have taken rather longer to join than he would have liked; he revealed on Tuesday that the negotiations for Sávio started three days after the end of last season. He believes they will be worth the wait.
Spurs have spent £304.5m this summer on Jan Paul van Hecke, Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes and Sávio. They have added Martin Dubravka, Andy Robertson and Marcos Senesi on free transfers.
summary: Manchester City have completed the signing of 18-year-old midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille for €95m plus €5m on a five-year contract, making him the most expensive teenager signed by an English club. Concurrently, City agreed to loan Omar Marmoush to Tottenham with an obligation to buy for an initial £50m and sold Nico González to Newcastle for £52m. These roster moves are part of a broader midfield rebuild at City, which has also seen the additions of Elliott Anderson and pursuits of other players.
key_points: Ayyoub Bouaddi joined Manchester City from Lille on a five-year deal for €95m plus €5m, becoming the most expensive teenager signed by an English club.
Omar Marmoush is moving to Tottenham on loan with an obligation to buy for an initial £50m.
Nico González has been sold to Newcastle for £52m as part of Manchester City's midfield restructuring.
Tottenham have also signed Sávio from Manchester City in a deal worth £75m plus £10m.

title: Omar Marmoush transfer news: Tottenham agree deal to sign Man City forward on loan with £60m obligation to buy
author: Lyall Thomas; Michael Bridge; Anton Toloui
content:
Omar Marmoush transfer news: Tottenham agree deal to sign Man City forward on loan with £60m obligation to buy
Tottenham have agreed a deal to sign Omar Marmoush from Man City; Spurs are set to sign the forward on an initial loan move with a £60m obligation to buy; Marmoush is set to undergo a medical ahead of following former City team-mate Savio to Spurs, who signed on Tuesday
Wednesday 26 August 2026 10:26, UK
Tottenham have agreed a deal to sign Omar Marmoush from Manchester City.
The Egypt forward is set for a medical ahead of completing an initial loan move with a £60m obligation to buy him permanently.
