title: Dutch Grand Prix: Lando Norris beats Kimi Antonelli at final Zandvoort race
author: Andrew Benson
content:
![Lando Norris kisses the Dutch GP trophy](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1024/cpsprodpb/540d/live/a65d7220-9f09-11f1-8ab2-7700e58d1417.jpg)
Lando Norris also won the Hungarian Grand Prix from pole position before the summer break
- Published
Lando Norris and McLaren beat Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli to take a masterful strategic victory in a compelling Dutch Grand Prix.
A topsy-turvy race started amid chaos as Max Verstappen crashed his Red Bull at high speed on a damp track at the end of the first lap, leading to a red flag.
Antonelli took the lead from Norris at the restart, but through two pit stops, Norris built a tyre offset to fight back and pass Antonelli for the win.
Lewis Hamilton was leading the race at the time, just ahead of the battling pair, out of sync on his pit stops, but Norris went past him further around the same lap to take the lead on track.
A late virtual safety car led to some team orders controversy at Mercedes as George Russell was ordered to let Antonelli past into second place, leaving him vulnerable to Hamilton.
But Russell, with help from a further late virtual safety car to allow marshals to recover debris on track, held Hamilton off to take the final podium position.
Further back, Fernando Alonso earned Aston Martin-Honda their first points since the incident-strewn Monaco race with an excellent drive on a one-stop strategy to ninth place.
The result leaves Antonelli with a 59-point championship lead over Russell, the gap unchanged from before the weekend.
Russell is on the same points as Hamilton, but classified ahead by virtue of his two wins to Hamilton's one. Norris, after his second consecutive victory, closes to 83 points off the lead, and now has to be a faint contender for the title if McLaren can keep their momentum.
The key stories of the first race after Formula 1's summer break were:
- A masterclass from Norris and McLaren
- Antonelli tightening his grip on the title by beating both his closest rivals.
- Team orders unhappiness at both Mercedes and Ferrari
- Further evidence that Aston Martin are making progress at last.
![Max Verstappen crashes at Zandvoort](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1800/cpsprodpb/6fda/live/9cf86260-9f06-11f1-8ab2-7700e58d1417.jpg)
Home driver Max Verstappen crashed out of the grand prix early on
Antonelli looked to have taken control of the race as he cycled from third on the initial grid to the lead after two standing starts punctuated by a long delay because of Verstappen's crash.
The Italian passed Russell for second behind pole-sitter Norris at the first start as the Briton was slowed by the inside of the grid being damper than the outside after a shower of rain.
But the race was stopped after Verstappen had an almighty accident at the end of the first lap.
Running too low through the flat-out final corner, Verstappen's inside wheels caught the wet painted line and he lost the rear, sending him nose first into the outside wall.
Behind him, Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto also lost control, but somehow he spun while staying on the track and was able to resume.
Verstappen was unhurt and climbed out with no problems as the field reformed in the pits while the track was cleared.
At the restart, the track now dry after a period of sunshine, Antonelli got the jump on Norris and moved into the lead.
Given his dominance at times this year, and the comfortable victory Russell had taken over Norris in the sprint on Saturday, that appeared to put the championship leader in control of the race.
The pair made their first pit stops together on lap 21, resuming in second and third place behind Hamilton, who delayed his stop by a further four laps.
But in the second stint, Norris came into his own. He closed in on Antonelli initially, and let the gap to within two seconds by the time the Mercedes driver made his second pit stop on lap 40.
This was Norris' chance. McLaren waited a further seven laps to make his stop and he rejoined only 4.8 seconds behind the Mercedes.
The pair closed on Hamilton together and the three were running nose to tail by lap 52. Two laps later, Antonelli feinted a move down the inside of Hamilton, but it didn't come off, and it left a space for Norris to leave his braking as late as possible on the clean outside line.
From there, he sailed around the outside of the Mercedes around the long, banked first corner, known as Tarzan, and set off after the Ferrari.
An error by Hamilton through Turn 10 later around the lap gave Norris a run out of the corner, and he drove past the Ferrari on the outside line into the chicane that followed.
That was the race won by Norris, even if there was a bit of jeopardy as McLaren chose not to pit under the VSC while all those bar Russell behind him did, but in the end he had more than enough in hand.
![Kimi Antonelli, Lewis Hamilton and Lando Norris battle on track in Zandvoort](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1024/cpsprodpb/2faa/live/15ebdd90-9f08-11f1-8ab2-7700e58d1417.jpg)
Norris is now fourth in the drivers' championship, 83 points behind title leader Kimi Antonelli
Antonelli passed Hamilton shortly after Norris just before a virtual safety car was called when Esteban Ocon's Haas stopped beside the track after Turn Three, and Hamilton and Antonelli both stopped for fresh tyres.
Hamilton had earlier complained about the team not asking his team-mate Charles Leclerc to let him by as he was trying to optimise his second stint and they were on different strategies.
And as Leclerc also stopped under the VSC, Antonelli, Hamilton and Leclerc all found themselves closing on Russell, who had not stopped.
Mercedes ordered Russell to let Antonelli by when he caught them, a request he fought against at the time, as he had wanted the pair to work together to protect him from the Ferraris.
Russell warned the team that they were risking a podium, and they probably would have lost it had it not been for a second VSC with two laps to go just as Hamilton was about to attack Russell.
The race did restart not long afterwards, but the breathing space it gave Russell was enough to secure the final podium place ahead of Hamilton and Leclerc.
Oscar Piastri took sixth in the second McLaren, ahead of Liam Lawson's Red Bull and Nico Hulkenberg's Audi.
Behind them, Alonso, who started 18th in the Aston Martin with its new Honda engine after a difficult qualifying session, had driven a masterful race.
The veteran Spaniard, who has still not decided whether to continue in F1 next year, ran a super-long 34-lap stint on soft tyres at the start, before switching to hards.
The final stages of the race saw him fighting to stay ahead of Alpine's Pierre Gasly and Racing Bulls' Yuki Tsunoda, closing in fast on much fresher medium and soft tyres.
But Alonso measured his pace to perfection to cross the line just over a second ahead of the Frenchman, with Tsunoda a further 4.7secs adrift.
After qualifying had left a confusing picture, Alonso's performance did seem to suggest Honda had made some form of progress with its engine to allow him to fight in such a way.
summary: Lando Norris secured a strategic victory for McLaren at the Dutch Grand Prix by overtaking Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton. The race featured early chaos, including a high-speed crash by Max Verstappen that brought out a red flag, and late tactical battles involving Mercedes team orders. With his second consecutive victory, Norris narrows the championship gap, while Antonelli maintains his lead over George Russell.
key_points: Lando Norris won the Dutch Grand Prix after passing Kimi Antonelli and Lewis Hamilton using a tyre offset strategy.
Max Verstappen crashed out of the race on the first lap, causing a red flag and a temporary suspension.
Mercedes used team orders to move Kimi Antonelli past George Russell into second place during a virtual safety car.
Fernando Alonso drove from 18th on the grid to finish ninth, securing Aston Martin-Honda's first points since Monaco.

title: Newcastle 2-2 Liverpool: How the players rated
author: Ciaran Kelly; Aadam Patel
content:
![Alexander Isak](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2560/cpsprodpb/9da1/live/1fbf33f0-9f15-11f1-b2a2-8945a27a2843.jpg)
Alexander Isak left Newcastle for Liverpool early last season
- Published
Dominik Szoboszlai scored a 99th-minute penalty equaliser for Liverpool in a dramatic 2-2 draw at Newcastle United, whose new manager Matthias Jaissle was denied victory in his first Premier League game in charge.
Here's how we rated the players - and then how you rated the players at St James' Park.
Newcastle starting XI
Lukas Hornicek: Solid Premier League debut. Made a flying save to get down to keep out Florian Wirtz's effort in the first half and pushed away Alexander Isak's header after the break. Calm in possession. 7
Amar Dedic: First outing for the club just a few days after completing a Â£30m move from Benfica. Made a crucial intervention in build-up to goal to slide in and hook ball away as Ryan Gravenberch looked to pick out Cody Gakpo. 7
Malick Thiaw: Wore the captain's armband in Dan Burn's absence. Battled. Looked to pick out William Osula with ball over top and put Liverpool under pressure. 7
Sven Botman: Was rusty in pre-season, but a little more assured here. Made one big block to get in the way of countryman Cody Gakpo's shot, but among those who backed off for Dutchman's goal. 6
Lewis Hall: Left rocked after conceding stoppage-time penalty following a coming together with Victor Munoz. Had dealt well with Ngumoha and coolly took ball off Isak's toe inside box at one point. 6
Lewis Miley: Only one half of pre-season action after recovering from a broken leg, but already such an important player. One particular crossfield ball to send Dedic down the right had supporters standing to applaud. 7
Sean Steur: Hard to believe he is only 18. Positive in approach in his first Premier League appearance even if his passes did not always come off. Composed. 7
Anthony Elanga: An opening-day miss against Aston Villa last season proved a sliding doors moment, but took his chance today. Coolly picked out the bottom corner for opener. 7
Yoane Wissa: Clearly relishing added responsibility from Jaissle in the number 10 position. Aggressive, sharp. Carried ball superbly to set up Willock's goal. 8
Harvey Barnes: Got nod ahead of Bazoumana Toure to start. Won a free-kick in a dangerous position with an enterprising run, but not involved enough. 6
William Osula: Led breakaway in build-up to Newcastle's first goal and made a sensible decision on when to release Elanga with weighed pass. Battled on with knock before coming off. 7
Subs:
Joe Willock (on 55, Osula): What an impact. Still had a lot to do for goal, but took it well. 7
Jacob Ramsey (on 55, Steur): Brought added energy. 6
Aladji Bamba (on 75, Miley): 6
Jacob Murphy (on 75, Elanga): 6
Fabian Schar (on 90+5, Wissa)
Subs not used: Jaouen, Shahar, Toure, Woltemade
Liverpool starting XI
Alisson: Arguably could have been in a better position for Anthony Elanga's goal. Could do nothing to keep out Joe Willock's strike. 5
Jeremie Frimpong: Poor display at right-back. Did get into some good positions down the flank but lacked that final delivery and picked up a deserved booking for tripping Harvey Barnes just outside the box. 4
Jeremy Jacquet: Encouraging start to life in the Premier League. Looks assured on the ball and has great passing range but must be more aware defensively. 6
Virgil van Dijk: Perhaps could have engaged earlier with William Osula in the move for the first goal but in truth, it was a wonderful run and finish from Elanga. Will know that Liverpool should not have let Joe Willock shoot for Newcastle's second goal. 6
Milos Kerkez: Struggled to keep up with Elanga for the goal and picked up a first-half booking. Did show some threat attackingly but has to improve defensively. 4
Dominik Szoboszlai: Was caught out of position for Newcastle's counter and this was an unusually average performance from the Hungarian but he took his penalty in injury-time brilliantly. 7
Ryan Gravenberch: Did well to create space initially but it was his pass that lost the ball just before Newcastle's opener. Made his 100th Premier League appearance and got the assist for Cody Gakpo. 6
Rio Ngumoha: Tried again down the right flank but it just did not click for the teenager, who scored the winner when Liverpool came here last season. A much tougher experience this time around. Replaced just after the hour mark. 5
Florian Wirtz: Was encouraging in phases and unlucky to be denied by a good save from Lukas Hornicek in the first half. Taken off just after the hour mark and will know that he must do more. 6
Cody Gakpo: Threatened and came close to scoring before unleashing a brilliant hit for Liverpool's first equaliser. Plenty of talk surrounding his future and this was a timely reminder of his quality. 8
Alexander Isak: Unsurprisingly booed whenever he touched the ball on his first return to St James' Park since his Â£125m move last summer. Looked pumped up but did nothing of note and wasted a brilliant chance at 2-1. Like Wirtz, must do more. 5
Subs:
Victor Munoz (on 63, Ngumoha): The winger who Liverpool beat Newcastle to signing looked sharp when he came on and won the crucial penalty. 7
Alexis Mac Allister (on 63, Wirtz): Came on to bring some stability playing in front of the backline. 5
Ronald Araujo (on 70, Jacquet): Did what was asked of him when he came on to partner Van Dijk. 6
Lewis Koumas (on 78, Gravenberch): 5
Subs not used: Mamardashvili, Endo, Tsimikas, Nyoni, McConnell.
How did you rate the players?
Player of the match
After the opportunity to rate players has closed, the score displayed represents the average from all the submissions by BBC Sport users.
summary: Liverpool secured a dramatic 2-2 draw against Newcastle United thanks to Dominik Szoboszlai's 99th-minute penalty. The result spoiled Matthias Jaissle's first Premier League game in charge of Newcastle, despite goals from Anthony Elanga and Joe Willock putting the hosts ahead. Cody Gakpo scored Liverpool's first equaliser before substitute Victor Munoz won the late penalty.
key_points: Dominik Szoboszlai scored a 99th-minute penalty to salvage a 2-2 draw for Liverpool.
Anthony Elanga and Joe Willock scored for Newcastle United in manager Matthias Jaissle's first Premier League match.
Cody Gakpo scored Liverpool's initial equaliser with a brilliant strike.
Substitute Victor Munoz won the crucial stoppage-time penalty following a foul by Lewis Hall.

title: Newcastle United v Liverpool: Premier League – live
author: Michael Butler
content:
78 min: Murphy’s first action is to leave a couple of studs in Mac Allister’s ankle. Yellow card for the Newcastle substitute. Free-kick for Liverpool in a promising position. The visitors use the break in play to make another change: Gravenberch for Lewis Koumas, a young forward and son of former Wigan midfielder Jason Koumas.
76 min: Newcastle make a double change: Lewis Miley and Anthony Elanga are replaced by Aladji Bamba and Jacob Murphy. Like-for-like changes in central midfield and on the right wing.
74 min: Wissa, arguably the best player on the pitch, wins a foul for Newcastle after slipping past Szoboszlai. Newcastle and their fans are beginning to glance at the clock.
72 min: Muñoz has made a real difference since coming on for Liverpool and he bursts forward from the right wing, feeding Szoboszlai. The ball eventually reaches Kerkez on the left but Liverpool’s left back doesn’t get his cross right. Isak was completely free at the back post and he doesn’t hold back when complaining to his teammate for that delivery.
70 min: Gakpo nods a cross perfectly into Isak’s path – 15 yards from goal and central – but the Liverpool No 9 leans back and launches a shot towards the away Liverpool fans, high in the stand. That was an excellent chance, albeit on Isak’s weaker left foot.
68 min: Hall gets free for Newcastle on the left, rolls a delicious low cross across Liverpool’s six-yard box towards Wissa … who steals a march on his marker … but fails to make any contact on the cross! Wissa only had to poke it past Alisson and it would have been 3-1!
66 min: Mac Allister has moved to the base of Liverpool’s midfield, with Gravenberch and Szoboszlai slightly more advanced. What that means is that when Newcastle counter-attack, Liverpool’s defensive midfielder is now one of the slowest players in the Premier League. Interesting tinkering from Iraola.
62 min: Two changes for Liverpool: Wirtz, largely ineffective, is hooked after an hour for Mac Allister. Víctor Muñoz, who reportedly was on the verge of signing for Newcastle before joining Liverpool, replaces the disappointing Ngumoha.
One minute after coming on, Willock gives Newcastle the lead again! It’s another surging counter-attack, this time led by Wissa, who somehow deceived three Liverpool defenders on the half-way line before releasing Willock. The Newcastle substitute received a pass from Wissa on the run, cut inside and somehow dug out a finish from 20 yards despite being off-balance. The ball curled past Alisson and kissed the far post before nestling into the net!
Newcastle United’s Joe Willock scores their second goal. Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/Reuters
Willock celebrates. Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/Reuters
56 min: Newcastle make a substitution: Willock and Ramsey on for Osula and Steur, the latter possibly at fault for not closing down Gakpo for the Liverpool goal. There were just 176 seconds between the Liverpool equaliser and Newcastle’s second goal.
After his sighter a moment ago, Gakpo makes no mistake with his second long-range attempt! After trotting infield from the left flank, the Dutchman finds himself completely unmarked between Newcastle’s midfield and defence. Gakpo has all the time in the world to turn on the ball, amble towards Newcastle’s penalty area, and fire into the far corner. Where was the Newcastle marking?
Cody Gakpo of Liverpool scores his team’s first goal. Photograph: Liverpool FC/Getty Images
52 min: Good play from Wirtz, who knits together a few passes in midfield, drawing Newcastle bodies to him before releasing Kerkez. The Liverpool left-back finds Gakpo, who curls a long-range juuuuuust over the Newcastle bar. That was close. Hornicek was nowhere near it, and it that was a yard lower, it was a goal.
50 min: Ngumoha, given a rare chance in the final third to run at Hall, instead tries to play a pass to the underlapping Frimpong, but instead passes the ball straight out for a Newcastle goal-kick. Eeeeeeesh.
48 min: Wissa shows another deft touch to get away from Gravenberch but the Liverpool midfielder recovers and hooks a foot around the Newcastle forward to make an outstanding tackle.
46 min:Liverpool immediately fashion a corner. They look like they have had a rollicking at half-time. The corner is flicked on at the near post towards Isak at the far … but Hornicek punches clear. That was a crucial intervention with the former Newcastle striker lurking.
Half-time reading: our snazzy men’s transfer interactive, which has news and details of all deals from Europe’s top five leagues, including Curtis Jones’ £25.7m move from Liverpool to Internazionale.
44 min:Liverpool look rather devoid of ideas. There are hopeful crosses, and shots from distance but this isn’t a fluid, attacking Liverpool side that was promised when Iraola joined. Credit must go to Newcastle for making it difficult. The home side have not stopped running, pressing at every opportunity.
42 min: Wissa trips Gravenberch in midfield and is a tad lucky to escape a second yellow card. It wasn’t a bad foul, but he did prevent a Liverpool counter-attack. Wissa receives what surely must be a final warning from Stuart Attwell. It remains 11 versus 11. For now.
40 min:Liverpool have had 10 shots to Newcastle’s five but have only tested Hornicek on one occasion. Much rests for Liverpool on Wirtz and Isak, and both have been quiet in this first 40 minutes.
36 min: “There’ll be a lot of cliches trotted out today about Kevin Keegan, and one of them will no doubt be that he ‘transcended his sport and his nationality’, but looking back, that’s actually true,” emails Justin Kavanagh. “As a schoolboy in Ireland, and definitely NOT a Liverpool fan, I really admired his tenacity and his attitude. I once broke my leg in France, and when the ambulance guys heard me speaking English, the first words out of their mouth was… ‘ahhh, Keveen Keegeen.’ Thanks for the memories Mr. Keegan.”
34 min: Frimpong is a good player, possibly not a right back, but his end product is often left wanting and butchers a Liverpool counter-attack here with a dismal attempt at a cross. Liverpool attackers were lining up at the far post but Frimpong effectively passed it to the nearest Newcastle player.
32 min: Newcastle have a promising free-kick for the latter foul, but Osula mimicks Szoboszlai’s effort by booting it straight into the wall. I’m surprised that Osula – given the No 10 shirt this season, by the way, is on free-kicks for Newcastle.
30 min: Bad news for Liverpool, as both full-backs – Kerkez and Frimpong – are booked within a minute of each other. Elanga will be keen to test Kerkez again, now that the Liverpool left-back is on a yellow.
26 min: Szoboszlai lines up a long-range free-kick, 30 yards out. This is his sort of range, but Liverpool’s star midfielder pings his shot straight into the Newcastle wall, which stayed strong and in unison.
24 min: Hall leaves Isak in a heap with a robust but reward challenge, which the Newcastle fans celebrate like a goal. The home side break forward, Wissa turning neatly in midfield, before the DR Congo forward feeds Osula with a remarkable trivela pass that Quaresma would have been proud of. Osula bursts onto the through ball but Van Dijk and Alisson just about do enough to prevent Newcastle’s striker from getting a clean shot on goal. The Liverpool captain very nearly put past his own goalkeeper, actually, but Alisson was alert.
Liverpool's Alexander Isak gets clattered by Newcastle United's Lewis Hall and Sven Botman. Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/Reuters
22 min: As if to prove my point, Kerkez overlaps Isak and gets free to the byline. The Hungarian has time to look up and zings a low cross towards Wirtz, but Hornicek reads it well to intercept, parrying clear, before Dedic hacks it away.
18 min: Fabulous save by Lukas Hornicek, Newcastle’s new keeper, to deny Wirtz! Kerkez had fizzed a hopeful low cross in from the left, Thiaw struggled with his clearance, and Wirtz pounced inside the area, pinging a finish through a crowd of bodies towards the far corner. Hornicek flung himself to his left and just tipped the shot around the corner! A save made all the better by the fact that it awkwardly bounced just before Hornicek got a big left hand to it.
Lukaas Hornicek makes a save.publications, games or single club/league/player publications. / Photograph: Paul Ellis/AFP/Getty Images
16 min: It’s been a really good start for Newcastle, but four players have particularly caught the eye. Elanga, obviously, but Steur and Hall have looked really tidy and Wissa has looked really busy in that No 10 role.
14 min: Looking back at that goal, Liverpool didn’t do too much wrong, in truth. Kerkez was well positioned and worked his nuts off to try and track Elanga. He simply couldn’t move his legs fast enough.
7 min: I’m not sure who the fastest player in the Premier League is these days – Micky van de Ven?! – but Elanga has to be up there. Kerkez is no slouch but he simply could not keep up with the Newcastle winger as he got on the overlap around Osula. Credit to Elanga for the finish, too, it was assured considering he was moving at such speed.
Cooooooorrrrrrrr, what a goal! Newcastle hit Liverpool on a devastating counter attack! Newcastle clumsily clear their lines but the ball bounces to Osula, who has room to turn and run at the Liverpool defence. Osula drives down the middle but has Elanga screaming past him to the right. It’s a simple through ball, but well executed, as Elanga streams away from the trailing Liverpool defence, takes a steady touch and arrows a finish low into the far corner! Lift-off at St James’ Park!
Anthony Elanga sprints clear and slides the ball into the far corner. Photograph: George Wood/Getty Images
Elanga scores his team’s first goal past Alisson Becker of Liverpool. Photograph: George Wood/Getty Images
4 min: The Newcastle fans are riding Isak hard, booing his every touch and rejoicing as Hall dispossesses the Swede as the Liverpool striker cuts inside.
2 min: A flowing Liverpool counter-attack starts with an excellent pass from Jacquet into midfield. Wirtz carries it forward, exchanges passes with Gakpo, and the German unleashes a fierce shot on the edge of Newcastle’s box, well blocked.
We are underway at St James’ Park. A new season for Newcastle and Liverpol begins with a kick-off for the visitors, taken by Isak. He is unceremoniously booed by the home faithful.
The tributes to Keegan continue, to the tune of David Bowie’s Heroes, just before the two teams come out onto the tunnel. Newcastle in their abomination barcode of a home shirt – how have they somehow butchered those splendid stripes?! – and Liverpool in a rather smarter red home strip.
There is a minute of applause for Keegan, raucously observed. Twice voted the greatest footballer on the planet, Keegan was a lot more to Newcastle United and Liverpool FC.
RIP King Kev. Photograph: Ian Hodgson/AP
A minute’s applause for the late Kevin Keegan. Photograph: Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images
“It’s very rare that deaths of famous people affect me, but Keegan was an exception: his passing stayed with me for days afterwards,” emails Chris Paraskevas. “It is difficult to surmise his importance to Newcastle’s history: I only witnessed his last ‘reign’ at the club, when he carried himself with his characteristic dignity and honesty during the Mike Ashley era, so the best parts of his legacy has been passed down or re-lived. His passing has only added to the massive sense of change / foreboding in the offseason, with Eddie Howe’s departure and the club’s plans to ‘be the best in the world by 2030’ revised to ‘best in the world by 3020’ (paraphrasing). When Pierre-Emile Højbjerg is turning you down, you know it’s going to be a rough season.”
Sky Sports have just shown a montage on Kevin Keegan and banners and tifos are now being shown around St James’ Park. I mentioned it earlier but there is a very moving mosaic of shirts on the pitch inside the centre circle – made up of jerseys left outside St James’ Park after the news of his death broke last month. Former players have flown in from all around the globe for his game, including Faustino Asprilla from Colombia.
I regret to inform you that I have gone. Legend is a term that is thrown around a lot, but King Kev was the definition of that word. RIP.
Delving into the Liverpool XI, there are two eye-catching selections.
Firstly, Rio Ngumoha: the 17-year-old looks like he is lining up on the right wing, with Cody Gakpo on the left. After Mo Salah’s departure, Liverpool have struggled to replace him during the transfer window, failing in their attempts to sign PSG’s Bradley Barcola and Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh (the Reds had a £50m bid for the latter turned down on Thursday). There is a real opportunity for Ngumoha to lay down a marker here and claim that spot for his own.
Secondly, Jérémy Jacquet has been chosen to partner Virgil van Dijk in central defence, despite the recent loan arrival of Ronald Araújo from Barcelona. Jacquet was really impressive in pre-season after his £60m move from Rennes was confirmed this summer. There are high hopes for the 20-year-old but many a promising young centre-back has come unstuck on his debut.
Jérémy Jacquet (left), Rio Ngumoha (centre) and Alexander Isak in the Liverpool warm-up. Photograph: Liverpool FC/Getty Images
Newcastle’s new head coach, Matthias Jaissle, speaks to Sky Sports:
It’s a transition phase. It’s a huge challenge. There will be some activities – hopefully – in the transfer market in the next week. But we are going to go for it [today], we will go all in. As soon as I saw Lewis Miley on the pitch, I was falling in love. He had a brilliant training week, we have to see if he’s ready for 90 minutes.
Here is a taste of some of the tributes to Kevin Keegan in and around St James’ Park.
Sir Kenny Dalglish (centre), Shola Ameobi and Bobby Moncur (right) lay down a wreath of roses in memory of the late Kevin Keegan at St James’ Park. Photograph: Owen Humphreys/PA
All of Liverpool’s players – here Víctor Muñoz and Alexis Mac Allister – were seen in the warm-up sporting jerseys in tribute to Kevin Keegan. Photograph: Liverpool FC/Getty Images
Artwork of the late Kevin Keegan seen on a street bollard as fans make their way to the match. Photograph: Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images
A Keegan shirt hangs inside Newcastle’s home dressing room, alongside the current first-time players. Photograph: Serena Taylor/Newcastle United/Getty Images
A card which will be used to create a tifo in remembrance of Kevin Keegan is seen on a seat. Photograph: Molly Darlington/Getty Images
Newcastle’s top-four chance creators from last season all have left the club. The club made well over £200m from the sales of Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães but it’s interesting that summer arrivals Bazoumana Touré (signed for £43m from Hoffenheim) and Aladji Bamba (signed for £30m from Monaco) are not in Jaissle’s XI today. Where are the goals going to come from?
Almost a year ago to the day, Newcastle’s first home match last season was also against Liverpool. With Alexander Isak holed up in his Northumberland mansion 10 miles south of St James Park’ as he attempted to force through a move to Liverpool, Newcastle conceded a 100th-minute winner, scored expertly by the Reds’ teenage star Rio Ngumoha.
A lot will depend on if Liverpool do any more business for wide players in this window (and how much Iraola trusts new signing Víctor Muñoz, who looks very promising) but this could possibly be a huge season for Ngumoha. The English winger has it all, he just needs the opportunities to prove it.
If there is a match between Newcastle and Liverpool, the mind instantly goes to Kevin Keegan. The man was a genius and King Kev will be rightly honoured today at St James’ Park as the two clubs meet. Tifos, banners and a 52,000-card salute is planned, while a mosaic has been designed to fit inside the centre circle, made up of shirts that were left in tribute by Newcastle supporters at the ground following the news of his death last month. RIP Keegan.
If talk of a club legend has dominated the historical discourse off the pitch, it is a much less popular, less permed individual that is a more defining figure for both clubs on this particular match.
Alexander Isak’s departure from Newcastle on deadline day last summer for a British-record fee was a huge factor in the north-east club’s poor campaign last time out that ultimately led to the departure of Eddie Howe. Isak’s sale was seen as a marker of ambition, or lack thereof, and that has permeated the club’s boardroom, the mindset of the fans and possibly Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães, all of whom have departed for pastures new. Newcastle are now a club firmly in transition under their new manager, Matthias Jaissle. Anything from Europe to relegation is on the cards.
If Newcastle are still trying to fill the void left by Isak, Liverpool seem still unsure how to best use the striker. Just as we do not know what Liverpool are capable of under Andoni Iraola, the jury is also out on Isak, who struggled for form and fitness in the last 12 months. With Hugo Ekitike still sidelined and Mohamed Salah departed, there is much pressure on the Swede for goals. Isak has the talent but there is still a question of whether he can produce the same output after his injury and in a team that is less tailored to the striker’s exact needs. Liverpool claim that they are still title contenders but they still seem short of elite squad depth in a merciless league.
The Premier League is back, and for these two clubs, this match should be an emotive and intriguing ride.
summary: Newcastle United secured a lead against Liverpool during a Premier League match at St James' Park. Anthony Elanga opened the scoring for Newcastle with a swift counter-attacking goal before Cody Gakpo equalized for Liverpool with a long-range shot. Joe Willock quickly restored Newcastle's lead following another fast counter-attack led by Wissa.
key_points: Anthony Elanga scored the opening goal for Newcastle United with a fast counter-attack.
Cody Gakpo equalized for Liverpool with a well-taken long-range shot.
Joe Willock restored Newcastle's lead shortly after coming on as a substitute.
Both teams made multiple tactical substitutions, including Liverpool bringing on Alexis Mac Allister and Víctor Muñoz.

title: Man City 2-1 Bournemouth: How the players rated
author: Shamoon Hafez
content:
![Rayan Cherki](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1200/cpsprodpb/ffab/live/d1460ab0-9f04-11f1-8ab2-7700e58d1417.jpg)
Rayan Cherki came on and provided two assists in Man City's comeback win over Bournemouth
- Published
Enzo Maresca's Manchester City came from behind late on to win his first Premier League game in charge. It was also Marco Rose's managerial debut for Bournemouth.
Below is how I rated the players, and then how you rated the players.
Manchester City
Gianluigi Donnarumma: Could do nothing about Bournemouth's opener but made superb saves to deny Justin Kluivert's low effort and Daniel Jebbison's flicked header. 6
Rico Lewis: Inverting into midfield from right-back, Lewis got forward and had an early effort saved but lacked quality overall before being taken off. 5
Abdukodir Khusanov: Missed a challenge on Rayan in the lead-up to Bournemouth's first goal and could not recover to stop the effort. 5
Ruben Dias: The new captain was culpable when conceding the opener too, failing to get his head on a long ball over the top. 5
Josko Gvardiol: Better at left-back or in the centre? Whatever the case, the Croatian was nowhere to be seen for Bournemouth's goal before popping up to score a cool injury time winner. 7
Marc Guehi: The England defender played in an unfamiliar holding midfield role but managed to score a late equaliser. With Ayyoub Bouaddi incoming, this experiment might only last one game. 6
Elliot Anderson: Club record signing Anderson showed glimpses of what he will bring to his new side, covering plenty of ground and often snuffing out the danger. 6
Antoine Semenyo: Looked bright in pre-season but unable to exert his influence on this game. 5
Nico O'Reilly: Deployed in the number 10 role, the England international created few opportunities of note and was taken off on the hour mark. 5
Phil Foden: Bright in the early stages, seeing plenty of the ball and playing a delightful flick for Lewis' chance but faded away. 5
Erling Haaland: Sporting a fresh new trim, the Norway striker somehow missed a sitter from a couple of yards out in the first half, while blazing over and scuffing another wide in the second. Has he lost his superpowers after chopping off his blonde locks? 5
Subs:
Matheus Nunes (on 56, Lewis): Nothing noteworthy. 5
Rayan Cherki (on 62, O'Reilly): Came on and changed the game for City. Provided two assists and will now be hoping to start on Friday at Crystal Palace. 8
Mateo Kovacic (on 62, Anderson): Should he have started in midfield instead of Guehi? 5
Jack Grealish (on 82, Foden): 5
Subs not used: Rulli, Marmoush, Gonzalez, Ait-Nouri, Reis.
Bournemouth
Djordje Petrovic: A diving save at full stretch denied both Haaland and Semenyo but beaten late on by Guehi and Gvardiol. 6
Adam Smith: The skipper kept Semenyo under lock and key throughout the game. 6
Antonio Silva: The Portuguese debutant looked comfortable as a ball-playing centre-half and showed he can mix it with the rough stuff against Haaland. Looks like being another shrewd signing but was yellow-carded for dissent. 7
James Hill: Continued his excellent form from last season by putting in a solid performance in the heart of the Bournemouth defence. 6
Adrien Truffert: Covered his centre-backs well to deny Haaland in the first half. 6
Alex Scott: A star in the making. The midfielder showcased why he has been linked with a move to City, displaying sublime composure on the ball throughout. 8
Lewis Cook: Nothing flashy, just a hardworking cog in Bournemouth's well-oiled machine. A real team player. 7
Marcus Tavernier: Coolly converted the opener at the back post to stun the home supporters and narrowly curled wide before half-time. 8
Justin Kluivert: Bournemouth's pacy frontline caused City issues and Kluivert was another menace. Unlucky not to score. 6
Rayan: Full of running and played a major part in the goal. Forced Donnarumma into a good save at his near post. 7
Evanilson: Picked out Tavernier perfectly with his low cross but was booked too. 6
Subs:
Tyler Adams (on 75, Cook): 5
Daniel Jebbison (on 75, Evanilson): Forced Donnarumma into a good save after coming on. 6
Alex Toth (on 75, Kluivert): 5
Ben Gannon-Doak (on 89, Rayan): 5
Subs not used: Dennis, Brooks, Diakite, Sanchez, Rodriguez.
How did you rate the players?
Player of the match
After the opportunity to rate players has closed, the score displayed represents the average from all the submissions by BBC Sport users.
summary: Manchester City secured a late 2-1 comeback victory against Bournemouth in Enzo Maresca's first Premier League match in charge. Substitute Rayan Cherki changed the game by providing two assists, leading to late goals from Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol. Marcus Tavernier had earlier opened the scoring for Bournemouth in Marco Rose's managerial debut.
key_points: Manchester City defeated Bournemouth 2-1 in a late comeback win.
Enzo Maresca and Marco Rose made their managerial debuts for Manchester City and Bournemouth, respectively.
Substitute Rayan Cherki provided two crucial assists to turn the match around.
Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol scored the late goals for Manchester City.

title: Formula One 2026: Norris beats Antonelli to win Dutch GP after Verstappen crash – live
author: James Dart; Yara El-Shaboury
content:
Norris wins the Dutch GP from Antonelli and Russell third
A great victory for the world champion, crossing the line some 11 seconds in front of championship leader Kimi Antonelli. And the final position on the podium goes to George Russell, who holds off the Ferraris.
Lap 70 of 72: There’s a good deal of debris around the Zandvoor track and this could give Russell a real chance of hanging on for third. Out in front, it’s still 11 seconds for Norris. He’s heading for victory. VSC is done.
Lap 68 of 72: This has been a mature drive from the world champion in a thrilling and chaotic race. He’s holding that advantage of 11 seconds. Hamilton is pursuing that podium but is just held off by his former teammate Russell.
Lap 67 of 72: Landon Norris has 11 seconds out in front after the frenetic pace. George Russell is third and battling to hold off Lewis Hamilton as they duel for a podium spot. It would seem more a matter of time for the Ferrari driver, but you never know.
Lap 62 of 72: Antonelli is catching up to Russell but Norris and Antonelli are lapping at the same pace. It is too early to say this is Norris’s to lose but he certainly has the advantage.
Lap 58 of 72: Norris: “Do you think we need to take it? Feeling a bit nervous now.” Too late, VSC is over. He leads by 6.2 sec from Russell, with Antonelli 6.3sec behind that.
Lap 56 of 72: Lewis Hamilton: “Are you using me as a guinea pig or what? What’s going on? How long will you have me stay out?” He pits for 3.1sec as Leclerc and Piastri also come in.
Lap 50 of 72: Norris is speeding, 3.2sec behind Antonelli now. Hamilton, in the lead, gets into a bit of a tiff over the team radio when asked what tyres they should go on next. “You have the data,” he replies.
Lap 43 of 72: Norris chooses not to pit for a couple laps in a row. Leclerc is called in, and he stays out and does not let a frustrated Hamilton through. Antonelli is in P4.
Lap 39 of 72: Leclerc is 1.3sec behind Russell, on tyres that are four laps fresher. Hamilton is 2.2sec away. Norris attempting to close in again on Antonelli.
Lap 35 of 72: Leclerc finally through after side by side with Piastri in turn 2. Hamilton then goes for the same move as his teammate, but gets through a tiny bit more easily as Piastri opts to defend less.
Lap 32 of 72: He does! Leclerc is rapid and attempts a similar move to what he did against Norris in the sprint race but Piastri covers the inside line.
Oscar Piastri leads Charles Leclerc. Photograph: Clive Rose/Getty Images
Lap 31 of 72: Norris is in overtake mode with now a 0.7sec gap on Antonelli. Leclerc and Piastri are in their own battle too with Leclerc about to pull a move …
Lap 23 of 72: Hamilton is on soft tyres here: is there a chance he only stops once while everyone else opts for a two-stop strategy? He tells his team that his tyres are OK.
Lap 22 of 72: Antonelli, Norris, Leclerc and Lawson all stop slowly. Antonelli and Norris lose half a second and Leclerc loses a full second. Hamilton now in the lead.
Lap 19 of 72: Antonelli is still on his mediums, leading by two seconds. Piastri has pitted from P3 to cover Russell but a 5.4sec stop is going to cost him.
Lap 15 of 72: Russell: “Consider original plan A.” Race engineer: “Copy.” Interesting. Plan A – whatever it is – needs to come into fruition quickly. Russell’s rear tyres are overheating now.
Lap 14 of 72: Piastri is really struggling on the hard tyre and is a distant third behind Antonelli and Norris. Russell is also falling away to Leclerc.
Lap 11 of 72: Hamilton has not been able to recover from his poor first start and is in sixth. Antonelli still has the lead and it is up to a second ahead of Norris. Leclerc only four tenths behind Russell.
summary: Lando Norris won the chaotic and thrilling Dutch Grand Prix after finishing 11 seconds ahead of championship leader Kimi Antonelli. George Russell secured the final podium position in third place after successfully holding off the chasing Ferraris. The race featured intense battles, pit stop strategy variations, and a Virtual Safety Car period following a Verstappen crash.
key_points: Lando Norris won the race by finishing 11 seconds ahead of Kimi Antonelli.
George Russell secured third place on the podium after holding off Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc.
The race involved strategic pit stops, tire management discussions, and a Virtual Safety Car following a Verstappen crash.

Oscar Piastri sits 1.4 seconds behind Russell, with both drivers running on hard tyres.

title: Manchester City v Bournemouth: Premier League – live
author: Emillia Hawkins
content:
15 min: Rayan goes for goal from the right side of the box and forces a save from Donnarumma. Bournemouth cannot follow the chance up from the resulting corner and City eventually clear.
13 min: Huge chance for City! O’Reilly makes a brilliant run down the left before crossing to Haaland in the box. However, the striker misjudges it and tries to bring the ball down with his chest, instead giving it straight to Petrović.
4 min: Big chance for City as the ball is played to Foden in the box, who brilliantly sets up Lewis with a clever flick. The full-back goes for goal but is denied by Petrović.
Ewen Atkinson has messaged in about City’s transfer business. He says:
“Pleased to see final confirmation of the arrival of the eye-catching teen tyro of an international Ayyoub Bouaddi, whose YouTube showreels prove that even while inexperienced and not yet fully physically developed, he has feet as sweet as Rayan Cherki and rides hard challenges like the best of ‘em - see, say, Maradona and Agüero and Haaland - I have wondered and pondered on the strange-seeming lack of news about City’s business of buying in the current transfer window, which of course is soon to close.
“So many out, but so few in. Saddened to see the backs of Rodri, De Bruyne, Silva, Stones and Ake, though less so about the exits of Savinho and Marmoush and the strongly rumoured going of Gonzalez. But that’s eight of last season’s named squad out, and as first teamers ‘only’ Anderson and Bouaddi in.
“Enzo Maresca is a disciple of Pep Guardiola, but is he taking the smaller squad principle too far?
“Or is the loss of Guardiola putting the best players off signing? We shall see, ey.”
“League is a marathon. Only sustained standards will keep you close to the top. I took the average standing of the top 5 who have won the league at least once in the last 20 seasons. The result is a surprise.
“Chelsea leads the table with 3.5 closely followed by City at 3.55, Man Utd at 3.65, Arsenal at 3.9 and Liverpool at 4.5. None of this will matter when Hull wins the league this season!”
A lot has changed in the Premier League this season. We’ve got some new rules, nine new managers and several big-money transfers. Sarah Rendell has outlined some of them below.
Eric Peterson has messaged in from the United States to say:
“Good morning from Pittsburgh! USA goalkeeping legend Tim Howard provided a remarkably wise ex-player’s perspective on the TV here about Pep Guardiola’s departure from Manchester City. When Howard joined Everton, during David Moyes’ legendary first tour of duty there, it was on arriving players to prove themselves to him. It was Moyes’ club. When Moyes left, the shoe was on the other foot, and it was on replacement Roberto Martinez’s shoulders to prove himself to the Everton players. This is the challenge Maresca faces in the Man City dressing room. Whether it goes as well as it did for Martinez at Everton or as poorly for Moyes succeeding Sir Alex at Man United, time will tell.”
Feel free to message in today with any thoughts, feelings, observations or predictions. Is Erling Haaland a shoo-in for the Golden Boot again this season? Will City challenge for the title in Enzo Maresca’s first campaign? Can Bournemouth pull off another shock? Let me know!
Marco Rose spoke positively before his first competitive match in charge of Bournemouth, at Manchester City on Sunday. The German head coach was unveiled in May after Andoni Iraola made the decision to leave the south coast club.
The Cherries are one of nine Premier League teams to have made a managerial change this summer and Rose knows what to expect up against Enzo Maresca, another of the coaching newbies this season.
“The things I saw so far with Chelsea and now Manchester City, it’s a clear idea, a clear philosophy,” Rose said. “You know what you get, you know what they want to play, you see the processes and the approach they have.
“It’s quite intense against the ball, high pressing and, with the ball, you know what quality you face and you see a clear idea in established play. It’s a tough challenge but we are quite positive. We had a really good pre-season. I settled in very well and everyone supported me and the new coaching staff.”
Bournemouth head coach Marco Rose during a training session. Photograph: Robin Jones/AFC Bournemouth/Getty Images
Enzo Maresca has brushed off the loss of Rodri to Barcelona for £65m by stating Manchester City will search for the “new Rodri” in the same way Sergio Agüero was replaced by Erling Haaland…
It has just emerged that Manchester City have agreed to sign Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille. The 18-year-old will join the club in a deal worth up to €100million (£85.5m) and is expected to sign a five-year contract with the option of another year.
Ayyoub Bouaddi is set to join Manchester City. Photograph: Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images
Speaking ahead of today’s match, Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca said: “At the beginning of the season you don’t set targets in terms of trophies. The target since day one has been quite clear with the club and the players, it’s to compete. You arrive in March and April to be there and then we will see what happens.”
Enzo Maresca during the Community Shield match between Manchester City and Arsenal. Photograph: Allstar Picture Library Ltd/Neal Simpson/Apl/Sportsphoto
As expected, Savinho is not in the Manchester City squad today as he closes in on a move to Tottenham. Omar Marmoush, who has also been linked with Spurs, has been named as a substitute.
It’s believed the duo could join the north London club for a combined £160million. Savinho will cost £85m while Marmoush has been priced at £75m.
Manchester City starting line-up: Gianluigi Donnarumma; Abdukodir Khusanov, Rúben Dias (C), Marc Guéhi, Joško Gvardiol, Rico Lewis; Elliot Anderson, Nico O’Reilly; Antoine Semenyo, Phil Foden; Erling Haaland.
Bournemouth starting line-up: Đorđe Petrović; Adrien Truffert, James Hill, António Silva, Adam Smith (C); Lewis Cook, Alex Scott, Marcus Tavernier; Justin Kluivert, Rayan, Evanilson.
Subs: Will Dennis, David Brooks, Ben Gannon-Doak, Tyler Adams, Bafodé Diakité, Juanlu Sánchez, Alex Tóth, Daniel Jebbison, Álvaro Rodríguez.
Hello and welcome to coverage of the Premier League clash between Manchester City and Bournemouth. Prem football returned on Friday and what a weekend it has been so far. Arsenal began their title defence with a 3-0 win over newly-promoted Coventry City, but the first Saturday of the campaign produced a few shocks…
Manchester United fell to a shock 2-0 loss to Hull City at the MKM Stadium following goals from Semi Ajayi and Nobel Mendy. Sunderland suffered a 2-1 defeat to Ipswich Town, while Brentford cruised to a 3-0 win against Tottenham. Elsewhere, Leeds United beat Nottingham Forest 1-0 and Everton clinched a 2-0 win over Crystal Palace.
Given those results, it is pretty impossible to predict which way this game will go. The last time these two sides met the points were shared in a 1-1 draw - a result which saw Arsenal confirmed as Premier League champions.
City will surely be looking for revenge today as they return to the Etihad Stadium.
summary: Manchester City faces Bournemouth at the Etihad Stadium in a Premier League fixture under new managers Enzo Maresca and Marco Rose. Early in the match, both sides create scoring chances, with Rico Lewis and Rayan testing the opposition goalkeepers. Prior to kickoff, Manchester City agreed to sign 18-year-old Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille for a fee worth up to €100 million.
key_points: Manchester City agreed to sign Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille in a deal worth up to €100 million.
Marco Rose takes charge of Bournemouth for his first competitive match following Andoni Iraola's departure.
Savinho is absent from Manchester City's squad as he nears an £85 million move to Tottenham, while Omar Marmoush is named as a substitute.
Early match action saw goal attempts from Bournemouth's Rayan and Manchester City's Rico Lewis, both denied by the goalkeepers.

title: Erling Haaland cuts off his trademark blond hair
author: Telegraph Sport
content:
![Erling Haaland](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/football/2026/08/23/TELEMMGLPICT000499295906_17874830073240_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bqsv7aT626_14DJUXhO54EUOknfLM6ja74Ig47ie2r9EE.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![Erling Haaland](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/football/2026/08/23/TELEMMGLPICT000499295906_17874830073240_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bqsv7aT626_14DJUXhO54EUOknfLM6ja74Ig47ie2r9EE.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
Erling Haaland has unveiled a dramatic new look after cutting off his trademark blond locks.
The Manchester City striker revealed his new buzzcut hairstyle on Sunday morning ahead of his side’s Premier League opener at home to Bournemouth later in the day.
“Short hair, don’t care,” he posted on Instagram alongside a range of pictures to plug the latest vlog episode for his YouTube channel, which has over four million subscribers.
Later in the episode, Haaland called a host of famous faces, including Oasis singer Noel Gallagher and former City manager Pep Guardiola, to get their opinions on his transformation.
Haaland, 26, has not sported short hair since his time at Borussia Dortmund, where he played three seasons before joining City in 2022.
Haaland removed his hairband during a 4-1 win over Arsenal in 2023 on a raucous night at the Etihad as City beat their title rivals to move one step closer to winning the league. There will be no need for one now, though, with a close-cut look to mark a new campaign.
![Erling Haaland](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/football/2026/08/23/TELEMMGLPICT000499290372_17874790028280_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqqVzuuqpFlyLIwiB6NTmJwfSVWeZ_vEN7c6bHu2jJnT8.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
It is a new-look City in more ways than one this term with head coach Enzo Maresca looking to kickstart a new era following Pep Guardiola’s exit.
Maresca is hoping for an immediate return to form in City’s Premier League opener after a chastening 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in the Community Shield last week.
So far, only Elliot Anderson has arrived but Maresca is hopeful the club will be active in the transfer market. Rodri has left for Barcelona while Savinho is closing in on a move to Tottenham.
“I’ll try to find a new Rodri – it is what it is,” the former Chelsea manager said. “Rodri, before he arrived here, he didn’t win the Ballon d’Or, he didn’t win the Champions League, he didn’t win the Club World Cup. Then he joined the club and then after he achieved many important things. Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri.
“When David Silva was here, everyone was worried - Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. When Sergio Agüero was here, everyone was worried – Erling [Haaland] arrived. When Ferdinando left, Rodri arrived. It’s just about this.
“When they leave, you need to be good and recruit the next one. They are all similar – David, Kevin, Fernandinho, Rodri, Agüero, Erling. It’s just normal, it’s a change. It’s not a problem, just go again and try to do the right things.”
![Enzo Maresca](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/football/2026/08/23/TELEMMGLPICT000498603545_17874787664970_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqFVq1ryR5wTJeBBSomGzQV0ikPYR0xYwuEBLwP9UFqPg.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Maresca added: “Hopefully we can do the things that we need to do,” Maresca said ahead of Sunday’s Premier League opener against Bournemouth. “It doesn’t help that there are players that for different reasons want to leave, this is for sure.
“But we need to adapt and we don’t want to keep players here that don’t want to stay.
“The normal thing in transfer windows is that you have to wait because all the clubs try to keep players until the last week and then sell for more money.
“It’s normal, I’m not worried about that. When the transfer window closes and we have all the squad there, for sure it will be different.”
summary: Manchester City striker Erling Haaland has debuted a dramatic new buzzcut hairstyle ahead of his team's Premier League opener against Bournemouth. The 26-year-old revealed his transformation on Instagram and YouTube, even calling celebrities like Noel Gallagher and former manager Pep Guardiola for their opinions. Meanwhile, new head coach Enzo Maresca is preparing for the season amidst squad changes, including Rodri's departure to Barcelona.
key_points: Erling Haaland cut off his trademark blond hair, revealing a new buzzcut.
Haaland showed off his new look on social media and his YouTube channel, calling figures like Noel Gallagher and Pep Guardiola for their reactions.
Enzo Maresca enters his first season as Manchester City's head coach following Guardiola's exit.
Manchester City faces squad changes with Rodri leaving for Barcelona and Savinho closing in on a move to Tottenham.
